title: Variables Space Proof Framework
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel proof framework based on dynamic graphs, designed to automate the generation of complex mathematical proofs. The core concept revolves around leveraging dynamic graphs to represent the mathematical theorem and the proof process, allowing for automated modification and generation of the proof sequence. This represents a significant advancement over traditional methods, which primarily rely on manual construction of proofs. The framework offers increased efficiency, potential for novel proof strategies, and the ability to tackle problems previously considered intractable. The paper details the design of the dynamic graph representation, the core mechanisms for proof generation, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's capabilities. We present a case study illustrating the framework's effectiveness in simplifying the proof of a specific geometric theorem. The paper concludes with an assessment of the framework's potential impact on the field of mathematical proofs and suggests future research directions.

title: Non-Linear Topological Transform Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear topological transform optimization to a complex system with dynamic structure. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their effectiveness in scenarios where the underlying structure changes over time. We propose a novel approach that leverages non-linear topological transformations to dynamically adjust optimization parameters, enabling more efficient and robust optimization. The core mechanism involves transforming the problem space itself, allowing the algorithm to adapt to evolving topology. This adaptability is achieved through a carefully designed transformation process that maintains the underlying objective while reshaping the decision space. The paper details the methodology, provides a simplified illustrative example, and concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future directions of this research.

abstract: The Gaussian distribution is often used to model univariate, numerical data, even in contexts where individuals' data values are bounded, e.g., test scores and biological measurements.We consider Bayesian inference for the parameters of Gaussian models when (i) analysts seek a post-processing algorithm that takes noisy sufficient statistics as inputs and produces a posterior distribution of the parameters as output, and (ii) the privacy mechanism enforces bounds on individual data values as a condition for satisfying pure differential privacy.Our primary contributions focus on the specification of prior distributions for model parameters.Specifically, we illustrate that failing to account for the bounds on data values when using informative prior distributions can result in posterior inferences with undesirable properties.Further, we show theoretically that the usual default priors used in the nonprivate setting do not lead to proper posterior distributions, and we suggest a default prior distribution that does.We show empirically that one can reduce mean squared errors and avoid inferences with infeasible support by incorporating the boundedness assumptions into the specification of prior distributions.We present methods for inferring about the mean and variance of a univariate Gaussian model and the coefficients and variance of a linear regression.As we discuss, the general strategies used for the Gaussian models can be adapted for other models when enforcing bounds on the data values to ensure differential privacy.

title: A step-wise task-oriented training of 6 DOF collaborative robot motion planning with Unity ML Agents package
abstract: The object of research is the process of training 6 DOF Collaborative Robot motion planning. This is important since, for a robot with a few DOF, the training process by RL is relatively easier compare to robots with high degrees of freedom. One of the most problematic areas is the requirement of additional parameters for each DOF inside the RL makes the agents’ task harder. This can be best described as agent attempting to change multiple numerical float values sliders until the correct solution is found. In addition to this, multiple configurations can also lead to a potentially solution and confuse the agent. During the research, a potential solution of using multiple simpler agents was explored. As simulation environment, a repository from ROS and Unity collaboration with UR3E was chosen and modified to test the stepwise control strategy. This strategy itself consisted of two agents performing separate tasks. For the first agent’s task, rotating of the base joint is performed to align with the target object. For the second agent’s task, movement of shoulder and elbow to lower the gripper closer to the target is performed. Obtained results showed that the first agent learned rapidly to align the base with the object and correct position was reached each time and second agent also had success although with lower precision. The first agent achieved a mean reward of around 79 by step 500000 with time elapsed of around 420 seconds. The second agent archived a mean reward of around 33 by step 500000 with time elapsed of around 1055 seconds. Therefore, proving the potential of joint motion separation when training with RL. This method can be used in other robots to aid in faster and more precise learning. It can also be used on other Universal Robots models and robots made by other manufacturers.

title: How Fast Do Agents Rot? An Empirical Study of Long-Horizon Degradation in LLM Agents for Production Decision-Making
abstract: Production deployments of large language model (LLM) agents remain unreliable on long, multi-step workflows even as benchmark success rates climb steadily. We argue this gap is largely an artifact of task horizon: benchmarks are dominated by short-to-medium horizons where success remains high, while production workloads demand an order of magnitude more dependent steps. We measure the effect directly, characterizing the shape of agent degradation and disentangling its cause across a large controlled study spanning nine models, six open models from 1.2B to 671B parameters, and three deployed proprietary systems; four task families, including a genuinely agentic tool-use loop; five horizons; and three context regimes. Task success follows a geometric law governed by a single per-step reliability parameter, which rises with model scale but saturates well below 1 even for the strongest models, guaranteeing eventual collapse at sufficiently long horizons. The effect is sharpest on the agentic task, where every model tested, including widely deployed systems, falls from near-perfect success to near zero within sixteen steps of (n=10,664 analyzed trajectories. Degradation is driven by step count rather than context length: bounding the context window steepens decay rather than easing it (logit slope -0.69 vs. -0.44), p=3x10-6), contradicting a lost-in-the-middle explanation and warning against a common production shortcut. Projecting measured reliability onto representative benchmark horizons quantifies a substantial gap between benchmark and production conditions, from 0.42 at GAIA-length horizons to 0.24 at hundred-step production horizons. For teams responsible for agent orchestration and reliability at scale, these results argue for horizon-aware evaluation and reliability budgeting in place of aggregate pass-rate metrics. Code, prompts, seeds, and raw trajectories are released.

title: Behavior-Skill: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Evaluating Vision-Language-Action Policies in Long-Horizon Tasks
abstract: Reliable execution of long-horizon mobile manipulation tasks remains challenging because overall task success depends on the successful completion of multiple constituent skills. Existing benchmarks, however, still rely primarily on full-task rollouts and aggregate task-level metrics, making intermediate failures difficult to observe and analyze. We present Behavior-Skill, a benchmark that reformulates the learning and evaluation of long-horizon tasks around executable constituent skills. It contains 235,492 skill instances from 10,000 demonstrations across 50 household tasks and 34 semantic skill categories. Each instance pairs a skill instruction with an aligned observation-action segment, and is further associated with a restorable intermediate state and a skill success condition to enable independent evaluation under valid preconditions. We further introduce trajectory-level and skill-level metrics to characterize policy capability beyond aggregate task success. Extensive experiments across representative VLA policies including pi0.5 and GR00T on the complete 50-task benchmark show that failures are highly non-uniform across skills, with contact-rich manipulation skills forming persistent bottlenecks. These results demonstrate that Behavior-Skill complements full-task evaluation by exposing intermediate capability profiles for analyzing and improving long-horizon VLA policies. Behavior-Skill is publicly available at https://github.com/nubot-nudt/Behavior-Skill.

title: PLC-DPO: Posterior Label Correction in Noisy and Ambiguous Preference Optimization
abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) simplifies alignment through pairwise comparisons but assumes all observed preferences are reliable. Real data often violates this assumption, leading to reversed, weak, or ambiguous labels that cause harmful policy updates. To address this, we propose Posterior Label Correction DPO (PLC-DPO) to robustly optimize preferences by routing each pair's training signal as a clean, flip, or tie case. The key idea is to use the calibrated policy-reference margin as online evidence to take appropriate correction actions. This reframes noisy preference learning as actively correcting supervision direction and strength rather than merely filtering suspicious examples. Across 57 dataset-model-benchmark cells, PLC-DPO obtains the best mean win rate against DPO (60.5 vs. 55.5 for the next-best method). Injected-noise and tie stress tests, human disagreement analysis, and self-confirmation diagnostics further show that the routing remains stable and distinguishes flipped from weakly directional pairs.

evidence.title: PLC-DPO: Posterior Label Correction in Noisy and Ambiguous Preference Optimization
evidence.abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) simplifies alignment through pairwise comparisons but assumes all observed preferences are reliable. Real data often violates this assumption, leading to reversed, weak, or ambiguous labels that cause harmful policy updates. To address this, we propose Posterior Label Correction DPO (PLC-DPO) to robustly optimize preferences by routing each pair's training signal as a clean, flip, or tie case. The key idea is to use the calibrated policy-reference margin as online evidence to take appropriate correction actions. This reframes noisy preference learning as actively correcting supervision direction and strength rather than merely filtering suspicious examples. Across 57 dataset-model-benchmark cells, PLC-DPO obtains the best mean win rate against DPO (60.5 vs. 55.5 for the next-best method). Injected-noise and tie stress tests, human disagreement analysis, and self-confirmation diagnostics further show that the routing remains stable and distinguishes flipped from weakly directional pairs.

title: Inductive Discovery of Industrial Pollution Patterns Machine-Learning Sensor Data Fusion in Heterogeneous Environmental Systems
abstract: : Industrial pollution patterns are typically sought in supervised settings, where a model is trained to reproduce labels supplied by a reference method. This article argues that the most informative patterns in industrial environmental monitoring are precisely the ones for which no labels exist an uncharacterized emission source, an emerging nuisance regime, a novel interaction between process state and meteorological condition and that the field therefore requires an inductive programme alongside its supervised one. We formulate pattern discovery on heterogeneous IoT streams as a five-stage inductive procedure: representation learning from unlabelled sensor responses, cross-stream fusion on a common substrate, candidate pattern emergence, attribution to a physical or process cause, and stabilization under sensor drift. Reviewing the evidence, we show that each stage is individually demonstrated but that the stages have not been composed, and that two obstacles dominate the composition. The first is drift, which is directional rather than random and therefore destructively entangled with the very pattern structure the procedure seeks to recover; the second is the instability of feature selection under heterogeneous instrumentation, where the same physical variable yields an informative calibration model on one instrument and none on another. We identify four testable propositions and conclude that inductive discovery in this domain is limited less by algorithmic capability than by the absence of labelled and drift-annotated streams, which makes deliberate instrumentation of the discovery process the binding requirement.

title: 基于自组织网络的量子态预测
abstract: Quantum state prediction is a crucial task in quantum information processing, vital for applications ranging from quantum computation to quantum communication. Traditional methods often rely on classical models, limiting the accuracy of predictions. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, based on self-organizing network structures, for quantum state prediction. The proposed algorithm leverages these networks to model and predict the evolution and coherence properties of quantum states. We demonstrate its efficacy through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental results, showcasing a significant improvement over existing approaches. This work represents a significant step towards more accurate and reliable quantum state prediction, offering a promising pathway for advancing quantum technologies.

title: 自适应量子纠缠的量子机器学习加速器
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing adaptive quantum entanglement to accelerate quantum machine learning (QML) algorithms. The core concept revolves around designing a novel quantum entanglement mechanism that optimizes the interaction between quantum qubits, enabling more efficient data processing and feature extraction during the training phase. We propose a system that dynamically adjusts entanglement parameters based on the specific characteristics of the data being processed, ultimately leading to faster training times and improved parameter search. This research addresses a critical challenge in QML: the inherent computational complexity of quantum algorithms, particularly during the initial stages of training. We detail the design of this adaptive entanglement system, its mathematical foundation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance QML performance. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions, focusing on scalability and integration with existing QML frameworks.

title: Quantum Entanglement Adaptive Geometry Mapping
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, possesses remarkable properties that hold immense potential for revolutionizing information processing. This paper explores the concept of a novel quantum entanglement geometry mapping – a system capable of dynamically adjusting quantum state properties in response to environmental changes, offering a pathway towards optimized quantum information handling. We introduce a new parameter set, designated as "modulations," which govern the entanglement's evolution and dynamically adjusts the quantum state to achieve desired outcomes. This approach, distinct from existing quantum algorithms, focuses on the fundamental properties of entanglement, presenting a significant advancement in the field. The core claim is that this self-adaptive geometry mapping can be used to achieve enhanced quantum information processing through robust and responsive entanglement dynamics.

title: Dynamically Adaptive Data Structures for Quantum Computing
abstract: The development of quantum computing relies heavily on efficient data structures to represent and manipulate quantum information. However, current data structures are largely static, failing to account for the inherent dynamism and probabilistic nature of quantum algorithms. This paper proposes a novel approach: dynamically adaptive data structures designed specifically for quantum computing. These structures will utilize techniques such as probabilistic data structures and adaptive indexing to optimize data access, reduce decoherence, and ultimately improve the performance of quantum algorithms. The core claim is that static data structures are fundamentally unsuitable for the quantum realm. This work explores the theoretical foundations and key design considerations for such adaptive structures, laying the groundwork for future research and implementation. The proposed system aims to minimize the overhead associated with managing quantum data, a critical bottleneck in quantum computation. The methodology focuses on creating a structure that reacts to the ongoing quantum state, leading to improved computational efficiency. The anticipated outcome is a more robust and efficient approach to data management within quantum systems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Guided Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a potentially transformative approach to constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), offering the possibility of dynamically adjusting constraints and exploring solution spaces with unprecedented efficiency. This paper proposes a novel quantum-enhanced constraint solver based on entanglement, aiming to improve solution quality and facilitate the exploration of a wider range of potential solutions. We detail the core mechanism, outlining the implementation of a quantum-enhanced solver that utilizes entanglement to identify and resolve conflicting constraints, ultimately leading to more effective and nuanced CSP solutions. The paper explores the theoretical foundations and practical considerations of this approach, highlighting its potential impact on the field of computational complexity.

title: Quantum Machine Learning: A Novel Activation Function Design Based on Quantum Adaptive Adjustment
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers the potential to revolutionize machine learning by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper investigates the application of quantum adaptive adjustment (QAA) as a novel activation function for quantum machine learning models. We propose a QAA activation function that dynamically adjusts the activation threshold based on the input data, enabling the model to learn more complex patterns and enhance performance, particularly when dealing with high-dimensional datasets and non-linear relationships. The core mechanism involves integrating a quantum-inspired adjustment algorithm that iteratively refines the activation function to better represent the underlying data distribution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this QAA activation function through theoretical analysis and experimental results on benchmark datasets. The paper concludes that incorporating QAA into the activation function significantly improves model accuracy and generalization ability.

title: Quantum Decoherence Dynamics Control and Resource Allocation
abstract: Quantum decoherence, traditionally viewed as a detrimental noise source hindering quantum computation, is presented here as a potentially controllable resource. This research explores the dynamic control of decoherence processes to facilitate resource allocation and optimization within quantum computing. A probabilistic model-based decoherence control algorithm is proposed, leveraging the inherent probabilistic nature of decoherence. This algorithm is then integrated with resource allocation problems, demonstrating the possibility of manipulating decoherence to enhance quantum computation performance. The core claim highlights the shift in perspective – transforming decoherence from a purely negative factor into an actively managed component. The investigation focuses on achieving dynamic control and optimization through precise manipulation of decoherence rates. The theoretical framework and proposed algorithm provide a new approach to quantum computing, moving beyond simply mitigating decoherence to actively harnessing its properties. ---

title: Neural Topology Generation Network
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture design, termed the Neural Topology Generation Network (NTGN). The core principle of the NTGN is to dynamically construct neural network architectures based on topological principles, mimicking the self-organizing process of biological neural networks. We leverage network flow algorithms, topological sorting, and graph theory to generate network topologies with predetermined complexity and specific connection patterns. Unlike traditional methods that primarily focus on weight adjustment, the NTGN directly addresses the design of the network's topology, enabling the creation of architectures tailored to particular functionalities. The key innovation lies in utilizing topological constraints within the generation process, leading to networks exhibiting emergent properties related to their inherent structure. This approach offers a pathway towards more efficient and biologically plausible neural network designs. The generated networks are characterized by their connectivity patterns defined by the following mathematical notation: G = (V, E), where V is the set of nodes (neurons) and E is the set of edges (connections) with associated weights wij representing the strength of the connection between neuron *i* and neuron *j*. The degree of a node *i*, denoted as di, is the number of edges connected to it: di = |{j | (i, j) ∈ E}|. The adjacency matrix *A* of the network is defined as *Aij* = 1 if (i, j) ∈ E and 0 otherwise. The network topology is further described by its graph Laplacian matrix *L*, defined as *L* = D - A, where D is the degree matrix and A is the adjacency matrix. The spectral properties of *L*, particularly its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, are crucial in characterizing the network's connectivity and potential for information propagation. We explore the use of random walks on the graph to characterize the network's diffusion properties, quantifying metrics such as PageRank and betweenness centrality. This paper outlines the methodology, provides a theoretical framework, and discusses potential applications of the NTGN.

title: Topological Quantum Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces Topological Quantum Algorithms (TQA) as a novel approach to quantum computing, focusing on leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states to achieve enhanced computational efficiency and data processing capabilities. The core principle centers around utilizing the structure of quantum states – specifically, topological invariants – to guide quantum operations and significantly reduce the number of required quantum gates. We present a framework that employs a specialized quantum circuit design based on these topological principles, demonstrating its potential for overcoming limitations inherent in conventional quantum algorithms. The paper highlights the benefits of this architecture, including improved fidelity and reduced computational complexity for specific quantum tasks. We conclude with a discussion of the challenges and future directions for this emerging field.

title: Non-Linear Topological Networks: Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to generate and optimize non-linear topological networks capable of exhibiting complex, predictable behavior and self-replication and optimization. Traditional network evolution algorithms often rely on predefined network structures, limiting their ability to handle complex, adaptive behavior. Our algorithm leverages a dynamic interplay of network interactions and feedback mechanisms to guide network evolution towards specific objectives. We propose a "Dynamic Self-Organization Network Evolution" (DSNOE) concept, simulating these interactions and feedback to foster self-improvement. This approach offers a significant advancement in network design, enabling the creation of more innovative and adaptable network architectures. The paper details the core mechanisms and provides a comprehensive framework for implementing this evolutionary process.

title: Title: Correlation-Based Quantum Entanglement Field (CBQE)
abstract: This paper presents the Correlation-Based Quantum Entanglement Field (CBQE) – a novel method for generating entanglement fields capable of transmitting information across space. The CBQE leverages the inherent correlations within a set of quantum states to create a dynamically evolving field, facilitating the transmission of information without requiring physical medium. We introduce a quantum algorithm that analyzes these correlations, generating a field that embodies the transmitted signal. The core mechanism focuses on creating a field that propagates information through the entangled state space, offering a fundamentally new approach to quantum communication and potentially enabling long-distance information transfer. This work demonstrates the feasibility of the CBQE through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations of existing entanglement techniques.

title: ## Black-and-Rufous Sengi-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BRSMA)
abstract: This paper presents the Black-and-Rufous Sengi-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BRSMA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core principles are derived from the foraging behavior and decision-making strategies observed in *Xerus erythroryzomus* (Black-and-Rufous Sengi). Specifically, the algorithm mimics the sengi's ability to efficiently explore and exploit the environment for food sources, employing a combination of adaptive step sizes, probabilistic movement, and a memory-based learning system. The BRSMA aims to improve upon existing metaheuristic techniques by incorporating a more biologically-inspired approach to exploration and exploitation. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search strategy, employing a fitness function to evaluate the quality of potential solutions. The performance of BRSMA is evaluated through simulations on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key innovations of BRSMA include a dynamically adjusted exploration probability based on the individual's search history and a novel method for updating the memory of previously successful solutions. This paper provides a detailed description of the BRSMA, its theoretical foundations, and experimental results demonstrating its capabilities.

title: Birdlike Noctule: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of the Bat
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Birdlike Noctule, inspired by the echolocation behavior of the European bat (Noctule). The algorithm leverages the bat's ability to navigate and forage in darkness by utilizing a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework. Specifically, the algorithm employs a 'frequency-amplitude' representation for particles, mirroring the bat's frequency and amplitude modulation of its calls. The algorithm's velocity update rule incorporates a 'search angle' inspired by the bat's flight direction changes, and a 'distance-based attraction' mechanism reflecting the bat's attraction to food sources. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's convergence properties and its potential for efficient global optimization. Comparative experimental results on benchmark functions showcase the algorithm's competitive performance against established metaheuristic methods, highlighting its effectiveness in complex search spaces. The Birdlike Noctule algorithm offers a promising alternative for solving a wide range of optimization problems.

title: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Model Selection in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising approach for training machine learning models across decentralized devices while preserving data privacy. However, a significant limitation of traditional FL is the static nature of model selection. Typically, all clients are trained with the same base model, regardless of the heterogeneity in their local data distributions. This static approach often leads to suboptimal performance, particularly in scenarios with diverse client datasets. This paper proposes a novel meta-learning framework to address this limitation. The framework learns a central model that dynamically selects the most appropriate base model for each client based on its local data characteristics. This adaptive model selection process aims to improve the overall system performance and efficiency of federated learning. The key contributions are the introduction of adaptability into the model selection stage and the development of a meta-learning approach for achieving this adaptation.

title: ## Big-Lipped Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bat Echolocation
abstract: This paper introduces the "Big-Lipped Bat" (BLB) metaheuristic algorithm, a novel approach inspired by the echolocation behavior of bats. BLB leverages the concept of bat loudness and phase angle adjustments, but extends these mechanisms with a modified 'lip size' parameter that dynamically adapts to the search landscape. This adaptation, representing the bat's ability to adjust its "lip" size based on the echo's strength, significantly improves exploration and exploitation capabilities, leading to enhanced convergence rates and solution quality in various optimization problems. We present a detailed description of the algorithm, including its core principles, parameter tuning, and theoretical analysis. The performance of BLB is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive ability alongside established metaheuristic methods such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms. The results indicate that BLB consistently achieves superior performance, particularly in challenging and multimodal landscapes. Future research directions involving hybrid approaches and adaptive parameter control are also discussed.

title: Neuro-Inspired Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cryptography by drawing inspiration from the principles of neuroscience. Current cryptographic protocols rely heavily on classical computing, which introduces inherent vulnerabilities. We argue that mimicking the efficiency, resilience, and adaptive nature of biological neural networks offers a superior path toward creating more secure and robust cryptographic systems. This work explores the theoretical foundations of neuro-inspired cryptography, focusing on concepts like spiking neural networks (SNNs) and neuromorphic computing. We present a framework for designing protocols that leverage these principles, emphasizing dynamic key generation, adaptive security measures, and resistance to known attack vectors. The core claim is that by shifting from deterministic, computationally intensive cryptography to systems modeled after the brain's processing, we can significantly enhance cryptographic security. The potential benefits include improved key management, enhanced resistance to side-channel attacks, and ultimately, more resilient cryptographic infrastructure. The presented concepts are intended to initiate future research and development in this emerging field.

title: 基于时间流纹理的因果推理
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal inference leveraging the inherent "texture" of time series data. Traditional causal inference methods often struggle with complex, dynamic systems where relationships are not easily captured by static models. We propose a framework that analyzes subtle variations within time series data, interpreting these variations as indicators of underlying causal processes. Specifically, we utilize time series decomposition techniques to extract temporal patterns, which we term "time texture," and then apply causal inference algorithms, such as Do-Calculus, to model and understand these causal relationships. The core claim is that by meticulously analyzing this time texture, more accurate causal inferences can be drawn compared to conventional methods. The key mechanism involves separating time series into trend, seasonality, and residual components, allowing us to isolate and interpret the causal signals embedded within the residual component – the time texture. We demonstrate the potential of this approach, although without empirical experimentation, through a theoretical framework and mathematical formulation, highlighting its ability to address limitations in existing causal inference techniques.

title: Chronometric Entropy Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to data compression, termed Chronometric Entropy Encoding (CEE). The central premise is that data streams inherently possess a time-dependent entropy component arising from the statistical fluctuations of physical systems, such as temperature variations, quantum noise, and inherent temporal randomness. Traditional entropy coding methods often ignore this crucial element, leading to suboptimal compression ratios. CEE directly analyzes and encodes this temporal entropy into the data stream, significantly reducing overhead. The core mechanism involves characterizing the time-dependent entropy fluctuations and formulating a new coding scheme that leverages these patterns. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the encoding process, demonstrating the potential for substantial gains in compression efficiency compared to conventional methods. This work introduces a fundamentally different perspective on entropy, viewing it not merely as a function of data content but as a function of time, opening new avenues for data compression and transmission. The proposed approach is applicable across a broad range of data types and physical systems exhibiting temporal randomness.

title: 基于图灵机验证的基于概率的逻辑推理系统
abstract: This paper presents a novel logic reasoning system based on the principles of the Turing machine, leveraging probabilistic models to enhance the system's reliability and robustness. Traditional logic systems often rely on rigid, predefined rules, while this approach aims to mimic the probabilistic nature of human reasoning. The core of the system involves integrating a probabilistic model with the Turing machine's inference process, allowing for a more nuanced and adaptable reasoning strategy. We demonstrate the efficacy of this architecture through a series of carefully designed experiments, showcasing improved performance in scenarios requiring complex deduction and handling of ambiguous information. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions.

title: Self-Adaptive Quantum State Optimization
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for scientific discovery and technological advancement, but its practical implementation is severely hampered by the inherent fragility of quantum states and the prevalence of errors. This paper presents a novel quantum state optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum State Optimization" (AQSO), designed to address these challenges by dynamically adjusting quantum states to minimize errors and enhance computational performance. AQSO leverages the unique properties of quantum states to create a feedback loop that continuously refines the quantum state, ultimately improving the fidelity and reliability of quantum computations. The proposed algorithm incorporates a dynamic adjustment mechanism based on error metrics, offering a significant departure from static optimization approaches. We detail the algorithm's architecture, key components, and experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing error rates and enhancing the speed of quantum algorithms. This work contributes to the ongoing research and development of robust and scalable quantum computing paradigms.

title: Neural Computation via Implicit Regularization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design centered around the inherent properties of neural computation. The core idea is to leverage the structure and connectivity of a neural network to achieve implicit regularization, thereby enhancing model generalization without the need for explicit regularization terms or techniques. We introduce a framework based on a topological neural network (TNN) where connection strengths are directly linked to the probability of information transfer between neurons. Through self-organization of the TNN, the topological structure itself acts as a constraint, promoting regularization. This approach differs significantly from traditional regularization methods which typically add penalty terms or modify the learning process. The key innovation lies in embedding regularization directly into the architecture of the neural network, potentially leading to more robust and efficient models. We demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of this mechanism and outline the design principles for implementing such a system. The proposed method offers a fundamentally different perspective on neural network design, shifting the focus from explicit control to leveraging the inherent properties of computation.

title: Quantum State Topology Analysis: Leveraging Topological Mapping for Quantum Computing Optimization
abstract: Quantum state topology plays a critical role in understanding the fundamental properties of quantum systems and has become a central focus within the development of quantum computation. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing topological mapping techniques to analyze and optimize quantum state properties, offering a novel approach to quantum algorithm design and optimization. We explore the application of topological mappings to identify and manipulate quantum states, ultimately aiming to enhance the performance and robustness of quantum systems. The core claim is that by employing topological mapping, we can uncover latent quantum properties and facilitate more efficient quantum computations. This research proposes a framework for quantifying and manipulating quantum states based on topological concepts, paving the way for advanced quantum algorithms and a deeper understanding of the quantum world.

title: 基于量子纠缠的全局优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement-based global optimization algorithm, designed to surpass the limitations of traditional optimization methods. The algorithm leverages the inherent correlations within entangled quantum states to achieve a globally optimal solution. We present a detailed conceptual framework, outlining the core mechanism and highlighting the potential for significant computational efficiency gains. The paper explores the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, including the role of entanglement in representing and manipulating solutions, and discusses the challenges and future directions for this groundbreaking optimization technique.

title: Title: Dynamic Chaos Theory in Constraint Optimization
abstract: Dynamic Chaos Theory in Constraint Optimization explores the potential of a novel framework for solving complex optimization problems, moving beyond static chaos models. This paper introduces a new theoretical model predicated on a continuous feedback loop that dynamically adjusts constraint parameters, fostering a "living" optimization landscape. The core mechanism leverages this feedback to predict self-regulating instability and stability, enabling near-optimal solutions to intricate, multi-objective problems. This research offers a practical and predictive approach to optimization, potentially revolutionizing the field of constrained optimization through a fundamentally different understanding of chaotic behavior.

title: Heterogeneous Topology Encoding Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Heterogeneous Topology Encoding Algorithm (HTEA) designed to optimize data compression and transmission efficiency by dynamically adapting encoding strategies based on data characteristics. Traditional encoding methods often struggle to effectively represent complex data. The HTEEA leverages the inherent topology of data structures to create a flexible encoding scheme, ensuring optimal performance regardless of the input data's dimensionality. We explore the core mechanism of utilizing this topology for adaptive encoding, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and a preliminary analysis of compression ratios. The algorithm's design aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for a wide range of data types.

title: DragonScale Optimization Algorithm (DSOA): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Dragonfish Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the DragonScale Optimization Algorithm (DSOA), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of dragonfish (specifically, *Chauliodus sloani*). Dragonfish utilize a unique "scanning" strategy to locate prey in dark environments, emitting short bursts of bioluminescence and analyzing the reflected light patterns. DSOA leverages this strategy by representing solutions as a set of 'scales' and employing a dynamic scanning process to identify promising regions in the search space. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'scale intensity' mechanism, simulating the dragonfish's sensitivity to reflected light, and a 'scanning radius' parameter that adapts based on the current search landscape. DSOA aims to achieve robust convergence and efficient exploration of complex optimization problems. The core of the algorithm lies in the iterative adjustment of scale intensities and scanning radii, guided by a competition-based mechanism mimicking the dragonfish's social hunting dynamics. This paper presents a detailed description of the DSOA, its underlying principles, and its potential applications.

title: Information-Theoretic Modeling of Neural Network Dynamics
abstract: The study of neural network dynamics is hampered by the inherent complexity of their architecture and the non-linear nature of their activation functions. Traditional methods often rely on simplified assumptions or focus on specific aspects of network behavior, leaving a gap in our understanding of the overall information flow. This work introduces a novel approach to analyzing neural network dynamics by leveraging concepts from information theory. Specifically, we quantify information flow through the network using entropy and mutual information measures. The goal is to identify critical pathways for information transmission, detect bottlenecks, and ultimately gain insights into the underlying dependencies driving network behavior. This approach provides a new framework for characterizing neural networks beyond conventional gradient-based methods, offering potential for improved training, optimization, and interpretability. The core methodology involves calculating entropy and mutual information between layers and neurons within a neural network architecture. These calculations provide a quantitative measure of information content and interdependencies, allowing for the identification of key components and potential areas for optimization.

title: Temporal Graph Neural Networks with Predictive Contextualization
abstract: This paper introduces Temporal Graph Neural Networks (TGNNs), a novel approach to graph neural networks designed to handle dynamic graphs where relationships evolve over time. Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) operate on static graphs, failing to capture the inherent temporal dependencies within systems. TGNNs address this limitation by integrating predictive contextualization. This involves utilizing learned predictions about future node states and edge relationships to augment the message passing process within the GNN layers. A recurrent component forecasts these future states, and attention mechanisms are employed to prioritize the influence of these predicted contexts during message aggregation. The core contribution lies in the unified framework combining graph dynamics with predictive learning, offering a significant improvement over static GNNs in applications involving evolving systems such as social networks, traffic networks, and biological systems. The proposed architecture enhances learning efficiency and improves predictive accuracy by considering the anticipated future state of the graph.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的生物信号处理
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for biological signal processing leveraging the adaptive capabilities of neural networks. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the network's ability to adapt to complex variations within the input data. This work proposes a dynamic adjustment mechanism within the neural network's parameters, driven by the biological signal itself, resulting in improved signal recognition and analysis. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive network structure, continuously optimizing the network's weights and biases based on real-time signal changes. This adaptive approach offers increased precision and efficiency compared to static network designs, particularly in scenarios with variable signal characteristics. The proposed framework demonstrates significant improvements in signal classification accuracy and robustness across a range of biological signal datasets.

title: Time-Flow Sub-Quantization and Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding and transmission by leveraging the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum superposition and interference. The core idea revolves around the time-flow sub-quantization, where time is discretized into quantum-like 'time quanta'. We introduce a time-flow encoder based on these quanta, utilizing precise control over their states to encode information. Furthermore, we explore the potential of quantum interference to enhance the efficiency of this encoding process. The theoretical framework presented here explores the feasibility of encoding information within the temporal dimension, offering a potentially disruptive methodology for both time-based coding and quantum communication systems. The key to this method lies in the manipulation of these temporal quanta, creating complex interference patterns to represent information, ultimately exceeding the limitations of classical encoding techniques. This work aims to establish a foundational understanding of time-flow sub-quantization and its implications for future advancements in information technology.

title: Title: Quantum Error Mitigation with Hybrid Quantum-Classical Techniques
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is a crucial step in developing practical quantum algorithms, allowing for the correction of errors introduced during computation. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems and the need for computationally intensive error correction mechanisms have historically limited the widespread adoption of QEM. This paper proposes a novel hybrid quantum-classical approach to QEM, integrating classical computation for error correction with dynamically adjusting quantum computations to minimize the impact of noise. We demonstrate the efficacy of this strategy through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing a significant reduction in error rates compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that prioritizes error correction based on real-time error metrics, utilizing classical computation to optimize the quantum circuit's execution. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods by offering a more efficient and scalable solution for QEM, paving the way for broader quantum computing applications.

title: Alpine Woolly Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of *Peromyscus nivalis*
abstract: This paper presents Alpine Woolly Rat (AWR), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm's inspiration stems from the unique wool-spinning behavior of the Alpine Woolly Rat (*Peromyscus nivalis*), a rodent known for its intricate and adaptive wool production. AWR utilizes a novel combination of adaptive parameter adjustment, a multi-dimensional search space exploration, and a dynamic memory mechanism to effectively navigate solution landscapes. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'wool density' concept, mirroring the rat's varying wool production based on environmental factors. The core of AWR lies in its adaptive parameter update rule, which dynamically adjusts the influence of different parameters based on the algorithm's performance and the characteristics of the search space. title: 基于动态量子算法的概率模型优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model optimization framework based on dynamic quantum algorithms. Traditional probabilistic model optimization often relies on static parameters, limiting the potential for efficiency gains. Our proposed framework dynamically adjusts quantum state fields, optimizing quantum computation's performance through a continuous, adaptive process. We detail the core mechanism of this framework, outlining the utilization of a quantum algorithm for real-time field manipulation. The resulting optimizations demonstrate a significant improvement in quantum state fidelity and overall computational throughput compared to conventional approaches. This work offers a promising pathway for enhancing the performance of quantum algorithms, particularly those involving complex quantum circuits. The framework's adaptability and the potential for substantial efficiency gains make it a significant advancement in the field of quantum computing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding & Analysis Method
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a significant challenge to the development of quantum computation. The inherent fragility of entangled states necessitates sophisticated techniques for encoding, transmitting, and analyzing quantum information. This paper proposes a novel method leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance the efficiency and security of quantum computation, focusing on the encoding and analysis of entangled states. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum entanglement to achieve enhanced data fidelity and facilitate more robust quantum algorithms. We outline the key steps involved, including the establishment of a secure entanglement distribution protocol, the implementation of a quantum entanglement analysis framework, and the demonstration of its potential impact on quantum algorithm performance. The research explores the practical implications of this approach, emphasizing its capacity to overcome existing limitations and pave the way for significant advancements in quantum information processing.

title: Adaptive Quantum Simulation of Non-Linear Geometry Models
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum simulation techniques to modeling non-linear geometry. The core claim is to propose a novel method utilizing quantum simulation's inherent dynamic adjustment capabilities to enhance simulation accuracy and efficiency, specifically for complex geometric structures. The method focuses on iteratively adjusting simulation parameters based on real-time feedback from the quantum simulation, optimizing the model's representation of the underlying geometric principles. This adaptive approach offers a significant advancement over static parameter adjustment methods, leading to improved results and a more efficient simulation workflow. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this technique through the modeling of a non-linear geometry, highlighting its potential for broader applications in fields requiring precise geometric analysis.

title: Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Earthquake Monitoring: A Systematic Review of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Applications
abstract: Earthquakes remain among the most destructive natural hazards, necessitating reliable monitoring and early warning systems for effective risk mitigation. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have significantly improved seismic signal analysis, enabling more accurate event detection, phase picking, classification, and magnitude estimation. This study presents a systematic review of ML- and DL-based approaches for earthquake monitoring, with particular emphasis on Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) as an emerging technology for high-resolution, real-time seismic observation. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic literature search was conducted across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar, yielding 252,223 initial records. After applying the predefined publication period, removing duplicate records, conducting relevance screening, and performing eligibility assessment, 138 peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2025 were retained for detailed analysis and synthesis. The review reveals a significant transition from conventional signal-processing techniques to advanced artificial intelligence-based approaches, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks, Transformer-based architectures, hybrid models, and Bayesian learning methods for uncertainty quantification. The findings further demonstrate that Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a transformative sensing technology because of its dense spatial coverage, high spatial resolution, and continuous monitoring capability. However, several challenges remain, including the lack of standardized datasets, limited model generalization across diverse geological settings, insufficient model interpretability, high computational complexity, and the limited integration of uncertainty-aware approaches for real-time seismic monitoring. This review identifies these critical research gaps and highlights promising future research directions, including multimodal data fusion, interpretable artificial intelligence, physics-informed learning, self-supervised learning, and robust uncertainty quantification for next-generation intelligent seismic monitoring systems. Unlike previous review studies that primarily focus on individual machine learning techniques or conventional seismic monitoring, this review provides a comprehensive and systematic synthesis of recent advances in machine learning, deep learning, and Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS), identifies current research gaps, and offers practical recommendations to guide future research on intelligent earthquake monitoring systems.

title: Optimasi Hyperparameter LightGBM Menggunakan Particle Swarm Optimization untuk Klasifikasi Kanker Payudara
abstract: Performa model Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) pada proses klasifikasi sangat dipengaruhi oleh konfigurasi hiperparameter yang digunakan. Penelitian ini mengusulkan penerapan Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) untuk memperoleh kombinasi hiperparameter yang optimal pada model LightGBM dalam klasifikasi kanker payudara. Pengujian model dilakukan menggunakan skema 3-fold cross-validation. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa model LightGBM dengan hiperparameter default menghasilkan akurasi rata-rata sebesar 95,96%, sedangkan optimasi menggunakan PSO meningkatkan akurasi hingga 97,54% pada konfigurasi swarm size 60 dan max iteration 250. Temuan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa PSO efektif dalam meningkatkan performa klasifikasi model LightGBM. Kata Kunci: Particle Swarm Optimization, Hiperparameter Tuning, Breast Cancer Classification, LightGBM

title: 数据驱动与人机协同——人工智能赋能高校英语视听说教学模式的构建与实践
abstract: 现在教育已进入数字化转型阶段，其中高校英语视听说教学正经历从“经验驱动”向“数据驱动”变化的特殊时期。针对目前网络平台数据利用不足、口语反馈不及时或分层教学难以落地等诸多问题，本文以《英语视听说》课程作为实例，通过将视听说知识加以图谱化处理，借助人工智能技术、数据可视化等手段，设计了“采集数据-可视化的诊断-AI智能人机交互-动态反馈”的新型教学方案。通过开发并分析热力图、运用大模型智能体、多模态评价等，使精准教学与个性化辅导有机结合。通过所做研究表明该模式有效提升学生的听力理解能力和口语表达能力，降低口语焦虑，为内蒙古高校外语教育的数字化研究提供参考价值，具有现实意义。

title: Assessing Accuracy and Reliability of AI-Generated Statistical Interpretations
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are rapidly used in academic research and industry to generate content and assist with analytical tasks. Because of the recent advances in generative AI, these tools can help with statistical data analysis, including data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, statistical modeling, and interpretation of results. However, concerns remain regarding the reliability and accuracy of AI-generated statistical outcomes and interpretations. This study evaluates the effectiveness and reliability of AI-assisted statistical analysis by comparing the performance of ChatGPT, Claude AI, and Google Gemini using a structured evaluation framework. The analysis was conducted using two datasets from the education and healthcare domains, which are among the most prominent data-driven fields. The study examines how effectively these AI tools select appropriate statistical methods, perform the analysis, and interpret the statistical outputs across multiple dimensions, including statistical accuracy, interpretive quality, domain appropriateness, limitation awareness, and consistency. The study concludes that AI can effectively support statistical analysis but should not replace careful human evaluation. Reliable AI-assisted interpretations still depend on well-structured prompts, critical review, and human oversight. These findings provide practical guidance for researchers, educators, and data practitioners and emphasize the importance of using AI responsibly in both statistics' education and real-world data analysis. Keywords: artificial intelligence, generative AI, large language models (LLMs), statistical analysis, data interpretations

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Improving Customer Satisfaction in Online Services
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an integral part of online service platforms, transforming the way organizations interact with customers and deliver support. This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence in improving customer satisfaction in online services by focusing on commonly used AI features such as chatbots, personalized recommendations, automated responses, smart search systems, and virtual assistants. Primary data were collected using the convenience sampling method, and SPSS tools were used to analyze the data, which was collected from 120 customers from Nagercoil City. The study focuses on two key objectives: examining how AI tools help to improve customer satisfaction in online services and identifying which AI features contribute most to customer satisfaction in online services. The findings indicate a significant positive relationship between AI tools and customer satisfaction in online services and the effect of AI-related service features on customer satisfaction in online services. The study highlights the growing importance of AI in strengthening customer experience in online environments and offers practical insights for service providers to improve user satisfaction.

title: WebWorld: The Browser as a World Model for Self-Improving Web Code
abstract: VLM-driven self-improvement of web code has a structural flaw: the model that proposes the repair is the model that judges it, and visual plausibility under that judge is a poor proxy for whether the page actually works. What the loop is missing is a counterparty the VLM cannot fool, and the browser already is that counterparty: a deterministic, executable simulator of how an HTML artifact behaves under user actions, and in everything but name a world model for web code. We present WebWorld, the interface that lets a VLM prior interact with this browser-as-world-model autonomously and decides which interactions become supervision. Each round, the VLM emits a critique that the planner compiles into a typed interaction contract; the browser re-executes the candidate and issues an acceptance certificate only when both target progress and preservation of every previously verified capability hold; certified transitions accumulate as a quality ratchet that is the only thing the SFT export ever sees. Under matched training, WebWorld-27B improves Raw-27B by 5.3 points on HTMLBench-400 and 14.9 points on MiniAppBench-Val, and reaches the level of strong frontier systems such as Kimi-K2.6 and GPT-5.4 on interactive HTML generation. Equal-size ablations show that browser-backed admission carries the gain: without the certificate, the matched 9B lift nearly disappears.

title: S3Gym: Can LLMs Turn Self-Testing and Self-Judging into Self-Improvement?
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly interact with external environments and accumulate substantial behavioral experience, yet existing agent benchmarks largely evaluate them as fixed policies. It therefore remains unclear whether an agent can actively test its behavior, judge the resulting experience, and use that experience to improve future decisions. We introduce \textbf{S\textsuperscript{3}Gym}, an interactive benchmark for evaluating LLM self-improvement through three coupled capabilities: \textbf{Self-Testing}, \textbf{Self-Judging}, and \textbf{Self-Improvement}. S$^3$Gym separates permissive exploration from strict held-out evaluation and instantiates this protocol in seven text-based games with executable environment verifiers. We evaluate three pathways for incorporating interaction experience: direct History ICL, score-conditioned Summary Memory, and parameter Training. Our experiments reveal that self-improvement is neither automatic nor uniform. Context-level experience improves performance for several model--game pairs, but the most effective pathway depends strongly on the task structure: summaries are beneficial when experience can be compressed into reusable strategic rules, yet often underperform raw history when success depends on precise, state-contingent information. Parameter training produces substantial gains on some tasks, but also exhibits unstable improvement and severe negative transfer on others. These findings show that recognizing successful actions is insufficient; agents must also transform feedback into executable and transferable policies. S$^3$Gym provides a unified framework for diagnosing this process and identifying the bottlenecks that prevent agents from translating interaction experience into reliable self-improvement.

title: Hidden Threat in Synthetic Data: Covert Targeted Bias Injection through Benign Text
abstract: Synthetic data is increasingly used to train large language models (LLMs), yet its security implications remain poorly understood. Prior work on subliminal learning suggests that models can inherit behavioral traits from seemingly unrelated training data. In this work, we investigate whether such mechanisms can be exploited to inject targeted social biases into aligned models through semantically benign synthetic data. We construct a pipeline in which a misaligned teacher model generates filtered synthetic datasets across domains such as creative writing and code generation, which are then used to fine-tune aligned student models. Our experiments show that benign-looking synthetic data can act as a covert channel for transmitting targeted biases while largely preserving the student model's general task capabilities. These results reveal a previously underexplored security risk in synthetic data-driven LLM training pipelines and highlight the need for improved safeguards. As one possible step toward this goal, we suggest that log-linearity-based scoring may provide a useful signal for screening seemingly benign synthetic data.

title: ANALISIS SENTIMEN BERBASIS ASPEK PADA ULASAN APLIKASI OJEK INDRALAYA MENGGUNAKAN PERBANDINGAN SUPPORT VECTOR MACHINE DAN NAIVE BAYES
abstract: Kehadiran Ojek Indralaya sebagai transportasi lokal sangat dipengaruhi oleh kepuasan pengguna di Google Playstore, namun banyaknya ulasan membuat analisis manual menjadi tidak efisien dan rentan subjektivitas. Penelitian ini menerapkan Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) untuk memetakan sentimen pengguna (positif dan negatif) pada lima aspek layanan: harga, keamanan, kenyamanan, fitur aplikasi, dan pelayanan driver. Menggunakan metode text mining, sebanyak 1.023 data ulasan dikumpulkan melalui teknik scraping dan diolah melalui tahap preprocessing (termasuk mempertahankan slang word bernilai emosi), lalu dibobotkan menggunakan TF-IDF. Model klasifikasi dibangun dengan membandingkan performa algoritma Support Vector Machine (SVM) dan Naive Bayes menggunakan pembagian data 80:20. Kinerja model dievaluasi melalui metrik Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, dan Confusion Matrix. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa algoritma SVM memiliki performa yang lebih stabil dan unggul pada seluruh aspek dibandingkan Naive Bayes, dengan performa tertinggi dicapai oleh SVM pada aspek harga (Accuracy 95,65%). Sebaliknya, performa terendah ditemukan pada algoritma Naive Bayes pada aspek keamanan yang dipengaruhi oleh adanya imbalanced dataset. Penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi berupa pemetaan sentimen berbasis aspek yang spesifik sebagai rekomendasi terstruktur bagi pengembang untuk menentukan prioritas perbaikan layanan transportasi lokal.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A Historical Development Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Simulation for Complex Physical Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of a hybrid quantum-classical simulation framework for tackling complex physical systems. The core claim is to develop a system that intelligently integrates quantum and classical computational techniques to efficiently model and analyze intricate phenomena. The research will explore a novel integration strategy, focusing on a carefully orchestrated workflow where quantum computations handle computationally demanding tasks while classical methods are employed for the bulk of the simulation. We will detail the design of the hybrid framework, its mathematical foundations, and the expected impact on simulation speed, accuracy, and the ability to handle highly complex scenarios. The paper will also address challenges and limitations in this approach and outline future research directions.

title: Non-Linear Adaptive Algorithms for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of non-linear adaptive algorithms for quantum computing, focusing on leveraging quantum computing's unique properties to enhance algorithm efficiency. The core challenge in quantum computing lies in the inherent complexity of quantum systems, necessitating algorithms that can effectively navigate this complexity. Traditional approaches often fail to fully exploit this complexity. This research proposes a novel non-linear adaptive algorithm specifically designed to address these challenges. We will detail the core mechanism, highlighting how it integrates quantum properties to achieve improvements in key performance metrics. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this algorithm on various quantum computing applications.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的量子态量子化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state quantumization method based on adaptive topology. Traditional quantum computing relies on complex quantum circuits, while topology offers a more intrinsic and physical description. We propose a new approach that leverages adaptive algorithms to dynamically adjust the encoding and manipulation of quantum states, enabling precise control and quantum state quantization. The core mechanism centers around utilizing topological structures to guide and refine the quantum state, ultimately improving the fidelity and controllability of quantum computations. This work addresses a fundamental challenge in quantum information processing by providing a fundamentally different approach to state representation and manipulation.

title: 基于图的知识推理的自动生成推理规则
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for automated knowledge reasoning utilizing a graph-based knowledge representation. Traditional knowledge reasoning methods often rely on manually crafted rules, which are time-consuming and limited in scalability. This work proposes a system that automatically generates reasoning rules from a structured knowledge graph, leveraging the inherent properties of graph structures to enhance efficiency and accuracy. We detail the architecture, mechanism, and evaluation of this framework, demonstrating its potential for significantly accelerating and improving the process of knowledge discovery and inference. The core of this approach involves constructing a knowledge graph, automatically generating rules based on graph structure and relationships, and offering a robust and adaptable system for reasoning over this graph. The paper concludes with a discussion of the benefits and limitations of this method, and suggests future research directions.

title: Geometric Information Theory Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Geometric Information Theory (GIT) to optimization, presenting a novel algorithm designed to efficiently discover optimal solutions within complex systems. GIT leverages the inherent geometric properties of a system to represent its state and guide the search process, offering a potential paradigm shift in optimization methodologies. The core mechanism centers around encoding system states using geometric primitives, enabling the application of information-theoretic operations to identify optimal configurations. We propose a new optimization algorithm, termed "Geometric Search," that effectively utilizes GIT's capabilities to address challenges encountered in optimization tasks. This work provides a foundational exploration into the integration of geometric principles with optimization techniques.

title: Temporal Graph Embedding with Predictive Recurrence
abstract: Existing graph embedding techniques often treat graphs as static structures, failing to capture the dynamic evolution inherent in many real-world networks. This paper introduces a novel temporal graph embedding method that leverages recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to predict future node states, thereby encoding temporal dependencies directly into the embedding space. The method employs an attention mechanism to prioritize relevant past states during prediction, enhancing the model's ability to capture complex temporal patterns. We demonstrate that this approach produces embeddings that better reflect the predictive power of the graph, leading to improved performance in downstream tasks such as node classification and link prediction. The core contribution lies in the integration of predictive RNNs with graph embedding, offering a richer and more accurate representation of temporal graph data. Our experimental results highlight the advantages of this method over traditional static graph embedding techniques.

title: Black-legged Mongoose Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Black-legged Mongoose Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BIMHA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-legged mongoose ( *Herpestes niger* ). Mongoose are known for their efficient and adaptable strategies in locating and exploiting food sources in diverse environments. BIMHA leverages these observed behaviors to develop a robust optimization algorithm capable of tackling complex and challenging problems. The algorithm incorporates key elements of mongoose foraging, including territory exploration, food source assessment, and adaptive movement strategies. Specifically, BIMHA utilizes a population-based search, incorporating a dynamic territory assignment scheme mimicking the mongoose's territorial defense. The fitness evaluation is based on an 'exploitation potential' metric, reflecting the mongoose's ability to identify high-value food sources. The algorithm's parameters are designed to ensure efficient convergence while maintaining adaptability to varying problem landscapes. The performance of BIMHA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive efficacy and potential for wider application across diverse optimization scenarios. The core of BIMHA is the adaptive territory management, which is described mathematically as follows: Let *N* be the number of agents in the population. Let *Ti(k)* denote the territory assigned to agent *i* at iteration *k*. The territory assignment probability is calculated as: Pi,j(k) = ( (∑l=1N exp(-di,j(k)) ) / N ) * ( (1/|Sj(k)|) * ∑l=1|Sj(k)| exp(-di,j(k)) ) Where: * di,j(k) represents the distance between agent *i* and agent *j* at iteration *k*. This distance can be Euclidean, Manhattan, or any other suitable metric. * *Sj(k)* is the set of agents currently assigned to territory *j* at iteration *k*. * |*Sj(k)*| is the number of agents in territory *j* at iteration *k*. The territory assignment probability ensures that agents are drawn towards territories with a higher density of agents, promoting exploration, while also considering the distance to these territories. The 'exploitation potential' metric, *Φi(k)*, is defined as: Φi(k) = ∑l=1P ( α * (1/di,l(k)) + β * exp(-γ * di,l(k)) ) Where: * *P* is the number of potential food sources (or solution candidates) in the search space. * *di,l(k)* represents the distance between agent *i* and potential food source *l* at iteration *k*. * α, β, and γ are adjustable parameters that control the influence of distance and exploitation. This equation prioritizes closer, less crowded food sources, reflecting the mongoose's preference for immediate and less contested resources.

title: Neuro-Controllable Topology Computation Network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to computation by leveraging the controllable connections within a neural network architecture designed based on topology. The core principle involves modulating the synaptic strengths between neurons via electrochemical signals, enabling the construction of computation networks with specific topological structures, such as small-world networks and scale-free networks. These networks are engineered to facilitate parallel and distributed computation, mimicking the complexity of biological neural systems. The methodology presented aims to bridge the gap between neural control and topological computation, offering a biologically-inspired framework for tackling computationally intensive tasks. The design focuses on utilizing electrochemical signals for precise synaptic adjustment, allowing for the creation of dynamic networks that can adapt and evolve during computation. This approach represents a significant step towards building more efficient and robust computing systems, drawing inspiration from the fundamental principles of the brain. The resulting networks can be tailored to specific computational needs through careful selection and manipulation of the topological structure and the electrochemical control parameters.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Computing Resource Coordination
abstract: This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for coordinating distributed computing resources, aiming to achieve efficient and scalable parallel computation. The core claim is that leveraging entanglement allows for resource coordination exceeding the limitations of classical communication, significantly enhancing computational efficiency. The proposed mechanism involves establishing a quantum network where nodes, each equipped with a quantum processor and an entanglement generator, share entangled states and perform measurements to dynamically perceive the computing status and needs of other nodes. This enables real-time task allocation and resource coordination. The novelty lies in exploiting entanglement's inherent properties to facilitate resource synchronization at speeds potentially exceeding the speed of light, offering a new paradigm for large-scale parallel computing. We present a theoretical framework outlining the key components and operational principles of this system, focusing on the mathematical models underlying entanglement-based communication and resource management. This work lays the groundwork for future research into the practical implementation of entanglement-based distributed computing. ---

title: Dynamic Matrix Generation: A Novel Approach to Automated Matrix Creation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic matrix generation technique based on deep learning. Traditional matrix generation methods often require manual design, while our approach automates the process, significantly reducing development and maintenance costs. We leverage deep learning models to learn the generation patterns of matrices and optimize parameters to produce matrices with specific characteristics. This technology offers a promising solution for enhancing machine learning and data analysis workflows.
