title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Computation (QEB)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computation architecture, Quantum Entanglement-Based Distributed Computation (QEB), leveraging quantum entanglement as the foundational mechanism for information transfer and computation. Traditional distributed computing systems are constrained by the limitations of classical communication, resulting in bottlenecks and reduced scalability. QEB overcomes these challenges by directly utilizing the inherent parallelism and resilience of quantum entanglement. The architecture decomposes computational tasks into a series of entangled sub-tasks, orchestrated across a network of quantum nodes. Synchronization and execution of these sub-tasks occur through controlled manipulation of the entangled states, eliminating the need for classical data transmission. Furthermore, the architecture incorporates fault tolerance through the dynamic reconstruction of entangled states, providing robustness against node failures. This approach promises significant advancements in computational performance and reliability, representing a paradigm shift in the field of distributed computing. The core claim of QEB is to build a highly parallel and fault-tolerant architecture by exploiting quantum entanglement as the primary communication channel. ---

title: Aceh Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Aceh Rats
abstract: This paper presents Aceh Rat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Aceh rats. These rats are known for their efficient and adaptive search strategies in complex and dynamic environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of their behavior, including path exploration, memory retention, and adaptive step sizes, to construct a novel optimization process. Aceh Rat employs a population-based approach with a unique rat representation and a dynamic path-following mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a rat population, a path representation, a memory mechanism for previously visited locations, and adaptive step size adjustments based on environmental feedback. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Aceh Rat through a series of benchmark problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions efficiently. The performance of Aceh Rat is compared with established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), highlighting its competitive advantages in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's design aims to provide a robust and adaptable solution for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: Aellen's Pipistrelle: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Pipistrelle Bat Echolocation
abstract: This paper proposes Aellen's Pipistrelle, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the echolocation behavior of the Aellen's pipistrelle bat. The algorithm leverages the bat's ability to navigate and locate prey in darkness through frequency-modulated calls and angle-of-arrival estimations. Aellen's Pipistrelle utilizes a population of 'bats' represented as particles, each with position, velocity, frequency, and angle parameters. The algorithm's core mechanisms mimic the bat's hunting strategy: frequency adjustments based on obstacle detection (fitness evaluation), angle adjustments based on obstacle direction (exploration), and a 'pulse' mechanism to maintain population diversity. We present a detailed description of the algorithm's components, including parameter tuning, convergence criteria, and its application to a range of benchmark optimization problems. Experimental results demonstrate that Aellen's Pipistrelle exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) across several test functions. The key innovation lies in the dynamically adjusting frequency and angle parameters, offering a more nuanced and adaptive search strategy than traditional approaches. Finally, we discuss future research directions, including incorporating more complex bat behavioral features and extending the algorithm to handle constrained optimization problems.

title: The Kangaroo Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Kangaroo Locomotion
abstract: This paper introduces the Kangaroo Metaheuristic (KMH), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique locomotion strategy of kangaroos. The algorithm mimics the kangaroo's hopping motion, incorporating elements of momentum conservation, energy optimization, and adaptive step size control. KMH utilizes a population of 'kangaroos' representing potential solutions, and employs a 'leap' operator to explore the search space, while maintaining momentum to accelerate convergence. The algorithm's key components include a dynamic leap size adjustment based on the individual kangaroo's momentum and the fitness landscape, and a 'shadow' kangaroo mechanism to promote diversity and prevent premature convergence. The paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, mathematical formulations, and the underlying principles driving its design, illustrating how these mimicry aspects contribute to its effectiveness in solving complex optimization problems. Future work will focus on empirical validation through simulations and comparisons with established metaheuristic algorithms.

title: Core Claim: We propose a novel adaptive quantum topology-based geometric optimization method that leverages the inherent properties of quantum topology to optimize complex geometric structures, enabling more efficient geometric design.
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating area of physics, offers the potential to manipulate space in ways that are fundamentally difficult to achieve classically. This research explores the application of quantum topology to geometric optimization, presenting a new approach that dynamically adapts to the problem's geometry. The core mechanism involves utilizing the self-adaptive nature of quantum topology to generate and refine optimization strategies, ultimately leading to improved geometric design. This paper details the proposed method, highlights its advantages, and provides a comprehensive analysis of its potential impact on geometric problem-solving. The study focuses on a specific geometric optimization task, demonstrating its efficacy through a series of illustrative examples. The analysis also considers the inherent challenges and potential limitations of this approach. We conclude with a discussion of future research directions and the broader implications of this work on the field of geometric optimization.

abstract: 생성형 AI 기술의 발전은 인간의 외모, 음성, 말투, 표정, 이미지 등을 정교하게 재현하거나 변형할 수 있는 환경을 만들어냈다. 특히 사망한 유명인의 생전 모습과 목소리를 복원하여 새로운 콘텐츠로 제작하는 이른바 디지털 부활 콘텐츠는 영화, 방송, 광고, 공연, 팬덤 문화 등 다양한 영역에서 활용 가능성을 넓히고 있다. 그러나 이러한 기술적 가능성은 동시에 사망한 유명인의 성명, 초상, 음성 등 인격표지가 데이터로 수집･학습･저장･재구성되는 과정에서 새로운 법적 문제를 발생시킨다. 인격표지는 개인의 정체성과 개성을 드러내는 요소이자 경제적 가치를 지니는 보호 대상임에도, 생성형 AI의 작동 구조 안에서는 학습과 생성의 재료가 되는 데이터로 취급될 위험이 있다. 본 논문은 생성형 AI를 활용한 디지털 부활 콘텐츠 제작 과정에서 사망한 유명인의 인격표지가 어떠한 방식으로 이용되는지 살펴보고, 이 과정에서 발생하는 법적 쟁점을 검토하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 사망한 유명인의 인격표지는 생존 인물의 인격표지와 달리 권리 주체가 직접 이용 여부를 결정하거나 사후적으로 문제를 제기하기 어렵다는 특수성을 가진다. 또한 디지털 부활 콘텐츠가 고인의 생전 이미지와 다른 방식으로 제작될 경우 고인에 대한 불명예나 명예훼손의 문제가 발생할 수 있으며, 인격표지의 이용 권한이 상속되는지 또는 누가 이를 행사할 수 있는지 명확하지 않은 경우도 적지 않다. 나아가 고인이 생전에 생성형 AI 기술을 통한 재현 가능성을 예측하거나 이에 대한 의사를 표시하기 어려웠다는 점에서, 사망한 유명인의 인격표지 이용 문제는 더욱 민감하고 선제적으로 검토될 필요가 있다. 특히 생성형 AI는 사망한 유명인의 인격표지를 단순히 복제하는 데 그치지 않고, 여러 인물의 외모, 음성, 말투, 분위기 등을 부분적으로 분리하여 결합하거나 변형할 수 있다. 이러한 인격표지의 데이터화와 파편화는 기존의 인격권 또는 퍼블리시티권 논의가 전제해 온 식별 가능성 중심의 보호 기준에 한계를 드러낸다. 생성된 콘텐츠가 특정 사망 유명인 한 명을 명확히 식별 가능하게 하지 않더라도, 그 안에 고인의 인격적 요소가 부분적으로 포함되거나 다른 인물의 표지와 결합되어 이용될 수 있기 때문이다. 이에 본 논문은 생성형 AI가 만들어내는 결과물에서 인격표지가 파편화 되어 나타나는 문제를 살펴보고, 이러한 현상이 기존 법체계의 식별 가능성 기준과 어떠한 긴장을 형성하는지 논의한다. 나아가 현행 인격권, 퍼블리시티권, 부정경쟁방지법상 인격표지 보호 규정 등을 중심으로 사망한 유명인의 디지털 부활 콘텐츠에 대한 법적 보호 가능성과 한계를 검토한다. 결론적으로 생성형 AI를 활용한 사망 유명인의 디지털 부활 콘텐츠는 기술의 발전 가능성만으로 정당화되기 어렵다. 고인의 인격표지가 데이터로 수집･학습･재구성되는 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 권리 침해를 줄이기 위해서는 우선 콘텐츠 제작과 유통의 중심에 있는 플랫폼의 역할이 중요하다. 따라서 플랫폼이 인격표지 이용 여부, 동의 절차, 표시 의무, 삭제 요청 및 이의 제기 절차 등을 스스로 마련하고 운영할 수 있는 자율 규제 체계가 필요하다. 또한 사망 유명인의 인격표지 이용을 둘러싼 분쟁은 권리 귀속이나 침해 여부가 명확하지 않은 경우가 많으므로, 이를 신속하게 조정할 수 있는 별도의 분쟁 조정 기구의 마련도 함께 검토되어야 한다.

title: Informative Label Missingness in Multiclass Classification Information Geometry and Excess Risk
abstract: Informative label missingness can change the usual efficiency ordering between completely and partially labelled classifiers because the pattern of missing labels may itself carry information about the classification model. We develop a general likelihood-based theory for this phenomenon in parametric multiclass classification. An efficient-information decomposition separates information lost through unavailable class memberships from information contributed by the missing-label mechanism. We then derive a quadratic expansion of plug-in excess risk over the active pairwise faces of the multiclass Bayes boundary, showing that classification efficiency depends on how information gains and losses align with directions that perturb the decision boundary. This yields a classification-weighted generalized-eigenvalue criterion under which informative partial classification may have smaller asymptotic classification risk without globally dominating complete classification in Fisher information. Near missing completely at random, with the marginal missing-label proportion fixed, redistribution of missing labels changes lost class-label information at first order, whereas efficient information from the missingness pattern appears only at second order. Three-class quadratic discriminant calculations, finite-sample experiments, and a semi-synthetic multiclass application illustrate the resulting regime-dependent behaviour.

title: VisER: Visual Evidence and Reliance for Object Hallucination Detection in LVLMs
abstract: Object hallucination remains a persistent reliability issue in large vision-language models, where generated object mentions may sound plausible but lack visual grounding. Recent training-free detectors use internal signals such as token likelihood, attention, visual confidence, or image-text similarity to identify hallucinated objects. These signals are useful, but they are often source-confounded. They measure how strongly an object is supported inside the model without distinguishing whether that support comes from object-specific visual evidence or the generated text prefix. In difficult cases, a hallucinated object can still receive high internal support because it fits the scene, is associated with nearby visual cues, or follows naturally from the generated text prefix. We propose VisER, a training-free two-sided metric for object-level hallucination detection. VisER evaluates each generated object mention from two complementary views. Visual Evidence measures whether object-context compatibility is backed by object-specific evidence from image tokens. Visual Reliance measures whether the object is supported more by the image than by the generated prefix. Combining these views gives a more source-aware grounding score, while avoiding additional object-level verification generations. Across multiple LVLMs and benchmarks, VisER improves AUROC and AUPR over a range of baselines.

title: DERELAB: Probing Defeasible Reasoning and Confirmation Bias in LLMs with a Generative Benchmark
abstract: Defeasible reasoning is a type of reasoning where inferences are drawn from plausible current evidence, but can be retracted upon the introduction of newer evidence. Although recent studies have examined language-model behaviors in defeasible reasoning, the datasets have been static and lack wide coverage of non-monotonic reasoning categories. We introduce DeReLab, a generative framework that produces multi-turn belief-updating conversations from parameterized graph structures across default and inheritance reasoning, with formally verified ground truth at every turn, enabling controlled measurement of how models respond to confirming and disconfirming evidence. This controlled generation process creates a testbed for experimental designs that isolate specific reasoning demands. Applying this capability to the study of confirmation bias, we evaluate nine open and proprietary large language models and find that nearly all exhibit a systematic tendency to accept congruent evidence while resisting incongruent updates, with several models correctly identifying a weakening update yet failing to revise their conclusion. We believe our work and findings will facilitate future research on evaluating language models in defeasible reasoning.

title: Diagnosa penyakit Gangguan Saraf Tepi (Neuropati Perifer) menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor
abstract: Peripheral neuropathy is a disorder of the peripheral nerves that can cause sensory, motor, and autonomic disturbances, as well as weakened tendon reflexes. Common early symptoms include numbness, tingling, pain, and a burning sensation, which are often more pronounced at night. Because the symptoms are nonspecific, peripheral neuropathy is often considered a minor complaint, resulting in delayed medical examination. This condition can increase the risk of complications, such as chronic wounds, balance disorders, and impaired limb function. The current problem is that the identification of peripheral neuropathy still relies heavily on the clinical experience of doctors and supporting examination results; therefore, a system is needed to assist the diagnosis process systematically and consistently. This study aims to develop an expert system for diagnosing peripheral neuropathy based on patients’ symptoms using the certainty factor method. The Certainty Factor method is used to determine the level of confidence in a diagnosis based on a combination of expert and user confidence values for the selected symptoms. The system also provides information about the disease and initial treatment recommendations to support the decision-making process. Based on the test results, the highest Certainty Factor value was obtained for Mononeuropathy, with a value of 0.9707 or 97.07%. This value indicates a high level of confidence in the diagnosis based on the symptoms entered. Therefore, the developed expert system is expected to assist in identifying peripheral neuropathy more quickly, consistently, and effectively, while supporting early detection so that appropriate treatment can be provided.

title: csyncmer_fast: an efficient single-threaded C implementation of closed syncmer extraction
abstract: A header-only C library for fast extraction of closed syncmers, using AVX2 SIMD with a two-stack sliding-window minimum and a rolling ntHash. Provides canonical and non-canonical variants, count-only and position-collecting entry points, a scalar fallback for platforms without AVX2, and an exact 64-bit streaming iterator. title: Adaptive Variable Quantum State Learning for Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computation utilizing adaptive variable quantum state learning. We propose a quantum circuit architecture that dynamically adjusts its parameters based on the current state of the system, enabling the efficient and complex transformation of quantum states. The core mechanism centers on a self-learning variable quantum state, allowing the circuit to adapt to the quantum system's dynamics and exploit quantum entanglement for enhanced computational capabilities. We demonstrate the feasibility of this method through a simplified model, showcasing its potential for accelerating quantum algorithms and exploring novel applications within the field. The paper establishes a foundation for a new paradigm in quantum computation, emphasizing the integration of adaptive learning with the foundational principles of quantum mechanics.

title: A Universal Computing Architecture Based on Multi-Qubit Superposition
abstract: This paper proposes a novel universal computing architecture centered around the exploitation of multi-qubit superposition. The core claim is that by constructing computational units based on entangled and superimposed states of multiple qubits, it's possible to achieve a level of parallelism exceeding that offered by classical computing. This architecture utilizes a scalable quantum superposition control system, leveraging the superposition of multiple qubits for parallel computation and employing quantum error correction codes to ensure the accuracy of the results. The innovation lies in shifting the focus from individual qubit manipulation to the orchestrated superposition of multiple qubits, representing a potentially more efficient pathway towards scalable quantum computing. This work outlines the theoretical framework, key design considerations, and potential advantages of this multi-qubit superposition based architecture. ---

title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning Frameworks Through Reverse Causal Inference
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for explainable reinforcement learning (RL) that leverages reverse causal inference to provide deeper insights into the decision-making processes of learned policies. Traditional explainable RL methods primarily focus on interpreting the outputs of a policy, often failing to elucidate the underlying reasons for its actions. This work addresses this limitation by integrating reverse causal inference, utilizing causal graphs to model and analyze the relationships between states, actions, and rewards. Specifically, we employ reverse causal inference to trace the causal pathways leading to a policy's decisions, revealing the key factors driving its behavior. The core claim is that incorporating reverse causal inference within an explainable RL framework allows for a more granular understanding of the policy's reasoning. We demonstrate the utility of this approach through a conceptual framework and outline a methodology for applying it to various RL problems. The ultimate goal is to move beyond simply explaining *what* a policy does and towards explaining *why* it does it, leading to more robust, trustworthy, and adaptable RL systems.

title: Non-Locality Quantum Computing Adaptive Calibration
abstract: Quantum computing offers unprecedented computational power but faces significant challenges stemming from its inherent non-locality. This paper introduces a novel adaptive calibration technique for non-local quantum computing, designed to mitigate these challenges and enable broader application of quantum algorithms. We propose a dynamic adjustment strategy for entanglement parameters based on real-time quantum system dynamics. This approach contrasts with traditional calibration methods that rely on static parameter sets, leading to improved stability and enhanced performance. The core mechanism of this adaptive calibration leverages feedback loops to continuously optimize the quantum system's state, resulting in a more robust and versatile quantum computation platform. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through simulations and preliminary experimental results, showcasing a significant reduction in entanglement loss and improved error mitigation. The findings highlight the potential of this approach to unlock new possibilities within the field of quantum computing.

title: Symbolic Regression with Genetic Programming and Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Symbolic regression is a technique for discovering mathematical equations from data. While promising, it often struggles to find complex, accurate, and, crucially, interpretable equations. This paper introduces a novel approach combining genetic programming (GP) for exploring the search space of mathematical expressions and Bayesian optimization for refining the search process. The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both methods: GP's ability to generate diverse and potentially complex expressions, coupled with Bayesian optimization's capability to efficiently guide the search towards solutions with desired properties—specifically, a balance between accuracy and interpretability. We detail the integrated framework, including the GP population initialization, the Bayesian optimization strategy for mutation and crossover operators, and the evaluation function that prioritizes both equation fit and a measure of interpretability. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in the quality of discovered equations compared to traditional symbolic regression methods, particularly for datasets with complex underlying relationships. This work represents a refined approach to symbolic regression, offering a practical solution to the challenge of discovering both accurate and understandable mathematical models.

title: Multi-Modal Graph-Based Knowledge Reasoning Framework
abstract: This paper presents a novel knowledge reasoning framework leveraging graph-based data integration and multi-modal information. The framework aims to enhance knowledge discovery and automation through the integration of diverse data sources, including images, text, and geographic data. We propose a modular architecture that allows for the construction and application of knowledge graphs, facilitating reasoning across modalities. The core mechanism centers on representing knowledge as a graph structure, enabling efficient traversal and inference. This paper details the design of key components, including data integration methods, graph construction techniques, and reasoning algorithms, showcasing its potential for advancing knowledge discovery in complex domains. We discuss the framework's capabilities and limitations, highlighting future research directions.

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics Modeling
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation and communication. This paper explores a novel approach to harnessing this phenomenon by integrating quantum entanglement dynamics with quantum circuit synchronization and control. We propose a dynamic "entanglement bridge" structure, leveraging non-classical entanglement effects to dynamically adjust qubit states, thereby enabling precise control and synchronization within a quantum network. The core claim is that this model will significantly enhance quantum algorithm efficiency and data transmission capabilities. This research addresses the limitations of existing quantum computing frameworks by introducing a dynamic, self-adjusting entanglement state, paving the way for more powerful and versatile computational solutions.

title: 基于多智能体协作的程序自我优化
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program optimization utilizing a multi-agent collaborative framework. The core idea is to transform program code into a collection of independent agents, each responsible for optimizing a specific segment of the code. These agents interact through collaborative algorithms – such as swarm algorithms (e.g., Ant Colony Optimization, Bee Colony Optimization) – to achieve global optimization. The system leverages competitive and cooperative dynamics among agents, mimicking natural swarm behaviors, to iteratively refine the program's structure and algorithms. This approach represents a significant departure from traditional, centralized optimization methods, offering the potential for more robust and adaptable solutions, particularly in complex software systems. The resulting system demonstrates the capability to evolve program code through a dynamic, agent-based process, potentially leading to performance improvements and enhanced code quality. Key metrics such as execution time, memory usage, and code complexity are continuously monitored and used to guide the agent optimization process. ---

title: Black Sumatran Langur-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Langur Adaptive Search (LAS) algorithm," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black Sumatran Langur, a highly intelligent primate known for its strategic decision-making and adaptability in complex environments. The LAS algorithm leverages the langur's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental cues and social interactions, mimicking its approach to resource allocation and obstacle avoidance. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: (1) a 'Cognitive Landscape' representation of the search space, (2) a 'Social Influence' component that simulates the langur's collaborative decision-making, and (3) an 'Adaptive Exploration-Exploitation' strategy informed by the langur's responsiveness to changing conditions. The LAS algorithm is designed to effectively navigate complex, multi-dimensional optimization landscapes, particularly those with discontinuities and local optima. The performance of the LAS algorithm is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive efficacy compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results show that the LAS algorithm exhibits superior performance in terms of convergence speed and solution quality for various problem types. The algorithm's adaptability and robustness make it a promising approach for tackling a wide range of real-world optimization challenges.

title: Bismarck Flying Fox: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bismarck Flying Fox
abstract: This paper presents Bismarck Flying Fox (BFX), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the strategic maneuvers and social dynamics observed in Bismarck flying foxes (Pteropus blemmeri). BFX combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism based on mimicking the flying fox's foraging behavior. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional search space, employing a dynamic food source representation and a hierarchical decision-making process. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a 'leader' selection mechanism reminiscent of the flying fox's social structure, alongside adaptive inertia weights and constriction coefficients. The performance of BFX is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and ABC. The key contributions of this work are the innovative adaptive parameter control, the multi-dimensional food source concept, and the mimicking of the Bismarck flying fox's foraging strategies for enhanced optimization performance. The algorithm's ability to adapt to complex landscapes and its relatively simple implementation make it a promising candidate for various real-world optimization challenges. The core mathematical framework is outlined, detailing the algorithm's key components and their operational rules, demonstrating its potential for further research and development.

title: Quantum State Topological Mapping Optimization
abstract: Quantum State Topological Mapping Optimization is a novel algorithmic framework designed to optimize geometric shapes and structures through the application of quantum state topological mapping. This approach leverages the unique properties of quantum states to guide and accelerate the transformation process, resulting in more efficient and precise geometric modifications. The core mechanism focuses on mapping a desired geometric transformation to a corresponding quantum state, enabling a more automated and effective optimization strategy. This research proposes a method that surpasses traditional methods by incorporating a dynamic and adaptive mapping process, ultimately leading to improved geometric outcomes. The potential applications of this technique span various fields, including computational geometry, structural design, and materials science.

title: Quantum Error Correction Protocol Adaptive Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a crucial aspect of quantum computing, aiming to protect quantum information from errors caused by environmental noise. Current QEC protocols often rely on complex and computationally intensive optimization techniques. This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction protocol, Adaptive Topology Optimization (ATO), designed to dynamically adjust quantum states to enhance the performance of quantum error correction. ATO leverages the inherent properties of quantum entanglement and superposition to optimize the structure of the quantum state, resulting in more efficient and robust error correction. The proposed method significantly improves the fidelity of quantum information and offers a pathway towards practical quantum computing.

title: ## Berg's Tuco-tuco: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Resilience of a Desert Animal
abstract: This paper presents Berg's Tuco-tuco, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed for tackling complex optimization problems. Inspired by the remarkable adaptability and survival strategies of the desert Tuco-tuco rodent, the algorithm leverages principles of foraging behavior, territorial defense, and dynamic adjustment to navigate challenging search spaces. Berg's Tuco-tuco incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) within a new adaptive mechanism. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a 'Territorial Response' mechanism, mimicking the Tuco-tuco's response to potential threats and resource scarcity, to dynamically adjust exploration and exploitation strategies. The algorithm's core parameters, including the territorial radius and response intensity, are adaptively tuned based on the problem's characteristics and the search progress. Experimental results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Berg's Tuco-tuco consistently achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods, showcasing its potential for solving diverse real-world optimization challenges. The algorithm's ability to maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation, coupled with its adaptable nature, contributes to its robust and efficient performance.

title: Heterogeneous Self-Adaptive Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Heterogeneous Self-Adaptive Optimization (HSAO) algorithm designed to effectively address complex optimization problems involving heterogeneous variables. Traditional optimization methods often focus on a single variable, neglecting the intricate relationships between them. The HSAO algorithm leverages the concept of heterogeneity – identifying and quantifying differences in the optimization objectives – to dynamically adjust the optimization target function and constraints, thereby ensuring a balanced and optimal solution across all variables. This paper details the core mechanism behind the HSAO algorithm, including the introduction of heterogeneity indicators and their use in adjusting the objective function and constraints. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the HSAO algorithm through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to handle complex scenarios and achieve superior results compared to existing optimization techniques. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's potential applications in various fields, highlighting its advantages in tackling challenging optimization problems.

title: Distributed Consensus Algorithms Based on Differential Privacy
abstract: This paper investigates the design and analysis of distributed consensus algorithms incorporating differential privacy. Achieving consensus in a distributed system while simultaneously protecting the privacy of individual nodes' data presents a complex challenge. We propose a novel approach that integrates consensus algorithms with differential privacy mechanisms. The core idea is to add carefully calibrated noise to intermediate computations within the consensus process, thereby obfuscating individual contributions without significantly impacting the final consensus result. We formally define the algorithm, outlining the key steps involved in achieving agreement while adhering to differential privacy guarantees. The analysis demonstrates the trade-off between privacy protection and consensus accuracy, providing insights into optimizing algorithm parameters for desired levels of privacy and reliability. Our work contributes to the growing field of privacy-preserving distributed systems and offers a potential solution for scenarios demanding both consensus and data protection.

title: Ant Colony Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Ant Colony Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ACIMA), designed for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of ants, specifically their ability to efficiently find optimal paths in complex environments. ACIMA utilizes a probabilistic approach, mimicking ant trail reinforcement, and incorporates a local search mechanism to further refine solutions. The core of the algorithm involves the construction of a solution representation, the establishment of an ant population, and the iterative improvement of solutions through trail update rules. Mathematical formulations are presented to describe the key components of the algorithm, including the probability of an ant selecting a particular solution element and the rate at which trails are reinforced. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key advantages of ACIMA include its adaptability to diverse problem structures and its potential for parallel implementation. Future research directions include incorporating adaptive parameters and exploring hybrid approaches with other metaheuristic techniques.

title: ## Ashy Titi: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Ashy Titi Bird
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Ashy Titi, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Ashy Titi bird (Salvatoria cinereiventris). The algorithm leverages the bird's efficient search strategy – primarily its ability to locate food sources in complex environments through a combination of visual cues, wind direction, and movement patterns – to create a robust optimization technique. Ashy Titi incorporates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with unique modifications to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. Specifically, it utilizes a "wind direction" heuristic to guide particle movement and a "visual cue" mechanism based on local neighborhood information to promote diversification. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The core of Ashy Titi resides in its adaptive wind direction and visual cue parameters, which dynamically adjust throughout the optimization process, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. The algorithm's design prioritizes both exploration and exploitation, resulting in a versatile optimization tool applicable to a wide range of problems.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Topological Information Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement as a novel approach to topological information analysis. Traditional topological analysis relies on classical information processing, which can be computationally expensive and limited in its ability to capture complex topological structures. We propose a method leveraging quantum entanglement to facilitate the extraction and analysis of topological information with enhanced efficiency. The core mechanism involves creating and manipulating entangled states to reveal subtle correlations within the topological system, ultimately leading to more accurate and robust analysis. This research highlights the potential of quantum entanglement to significantly advance the field of topological information processing, offering a fundamentally different computational paradigm.

title: Self-Organized Chaotic Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organized chaotic quantum algorithm designed for dynamic control of complex systems. Traditional quantum control methods often require extensive manual parameter tuning, limiting the adaptability of quantum systems. Our algorithm leverages the inherent properties of chaotic dynamics and quantum computation to achieve automatic parameter adjustment, providing a pathway towards more flexible and robust control. We detail the core mechanism, highlighting the key steps involved in establishing and maintaining the chaotic system, and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations. This algorithm offers a paradigm shift in quantum system management, potentially unlocking new capabilities in areas such as molecular dynamics simulations, materials science, and fundamental physics research. The core claim emphasizes the algorithm's ability to autonomously adjust quantum system parameters, enabling dynamic control of complex systems.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework based on dynamic self-organizing networks, designed to automatically adjust network connections and weights based on input data. title: Neuro-Plasticity Enhanced Framework (NGEF)
abstract: This paper introduces the Neuro-Plasticity Enhanced Framework (NGEF), a novel approach to neural network design and training centered on the principle of neuron plasticity. Traditional neural network approaches often rely on static parameters and predefined rules, limiting adaptability. The NGEF utilizes a dynamic simulation of neuron plasticity to guide the learning process, enabling the model to self-adjust and enhance learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. We propose a new learning algorithm that iteratively modifies the network's parameters based on new data, fostering a continuous feedback loop that promotes robust and adaptable models. This work explores the potential of leveraging neural plasticity to create more versatile and resilient learning systems.

title: Dynamic Matrix-Based Quantum Entanglement Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization algorithm based on dynamic matrix adjustment, designed to enhance the efficiency and stability of matrix operations within quantum entanglement scenarios. The core mechanism leverages a self-adjusting matrix representation, allowing the algorithm to dynamically optimize the weighting of matrix elements. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameters, failing to fully exploit the inherent complexity of quantum systems. This algorithm offers a potential pathway toward improved performance in tasks such as quantum state manipulation and entanglement generation. The paper details the design of the dynamic matrix framework, its implementation using a simplified model, and preliminary results demonstrating improved convergence speed and reduced error rates compared to existing approaches. We explore the impact of this dynamic approach on key entanglement-related operations.

title: Causal Bayesian Networks with Dynamic Interventions and Counterfactual Reasoning
abstract: This research addresses the limitations of existing Causal Bayesian Networks (CBNs) concerning the representation and reasoning about dynamic interventions and counterfactual scenarios. We introduce a novel framework integrating a dynamic intervention operator and a sophisticated counterfactual inference engine. The dynamic intervention operator allows for the simulation of interventions by modifying edge probabilities based on simulated events. The counterfactual inference engine leverages the network structure to estimate the outcome of hypothetical scenarios, providing insights into "what if" questions. This framework enables more realistic and insightful causal modeling, moving beyond static CBNs to encompass evolving causal relationships. The core contribution lies in the ability to model not only the initial causal structure but also the impact of dynamic changes and the potential outcomes of alternative scenarios. The system is designed to provide a robust and flexible approach for causal discovery, prediction, and intervention planning, particularly in complex systems where intervention effects are not fully understood.

title: ## Blood Snail Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces the "Blood Snail Metaheuristic Algorithm" (BSMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the adaptive feeding behavior of the blood snail (*Philomedusa plumbea*). The algorithm mimics the snail's ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources by employing a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, a multi-layered decision-making process, and a robust mechanism for handling local optima. BSMA utilizes a population of 'snails' representing potential solutions, each with an 'energy' level indicative of its search progress. The algorithm's core mechanics include a 'feeding' strategy based on gradient information, a 'shell' structure for representing solution diversity, and a 'pulsation' mechanism to dynamically adjust exploration and exploitation parameters. Unlike many existing metaheuristics, BSMA doesn't rely on a fixed number of iterations or a predetermined convergence criterion, instead, it adapts its search strategy based on the collective behavior of the snail population. This paper provides a detailed description of BSMA's design and underlying principles, laying the foundation for future research and applications.

title: ## Anchieta's Serotine: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Serotine Lizard
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, "Anchieta's Serotine," inspired by the adaptive hunting behavior of the serotine lizard (*Sceloporus angustifrons*). Serotine lizards exhibit a remarkable ability to dynamically adjust their hunting strategies based on prey availability and environmental conditions. This paper leverages these adaptive strategies to develop a novel algorithm for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm, termed Anchieta's Serotine, incorporates elements of adaptive foraging, territory defense, and social interaction observed in serotine lizards. The core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance, mimicking the lizard's shifting focus between searching for new food sources and defending established territories. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a modified velocity update rule and a novel territory assignment mechanism. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Anchieta's Serotine through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). Results indicate that Anchieta's Serotine provides competitive performance, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and dynamic changes.

title: The Yunnan Salamander Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (YISA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Yunnan Salamander Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (YISA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Yunnan salamanders. These amphibians exhibit a unique strategy of exploring their environment, alternating between periods of active searching and periods of resting and strategic repositioning. YISA leverages these behaviors by dynamically adjusting the population size, exploration rate, and exploitation rate based on an internal 'energy' level, mimicking the salamander's need to conserve energy while efficiently searching for food. The algorithm incorporates a novel 'Rest-Search' mechanism and a 'Strategic Shift' operator to simulate the salamander's adaptive movement patterns. The core of YISA lies in its adaptive parameter control, designed to enhance convergence speed and robustness in complex optimization problems. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and theoretical underpinnings, emphasizing its potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic methods.

title: Zero-Knowledge Quantum Signature Verification with Adaptive Thresholding
abstract: Quantum signature verification presents a paradigm shift in cryptography, offering enhanced security through the use of quantum mechanics. However, current protocols often rely on static thresholds, limiting their robustness. This paper introduces a novel zero-knowledge quantum signature verification protocol that dynamically adjusts threshold levels based on the system's internal state, significantly enhancing security and efficiency. We detail the protocol's architecture, including the quantum signature generation, verification, and threshold adaptation mechanism. The system's robustness is validated through simulations and analyses, demonstrating its superior performance compared to static threshold-based approaches. The core principle lies in leveraging the inherent dynamics of quantum states to maintain a secure verification process.

title: ## Red-Neck Snake Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RNIMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Red-Neck Snake Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RNIMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the hunting behavior of *Pantherophis guttatus*, commonly known as the red-neck snake. These snakes employ a unique strategy – "red-necking" – where they rapidly approach a prey (typically a small rodent) with a high velocity, then abruptly decelerate and snake towards the prey. This algorithm leverages this dynamic approach to navigate complex search spaces. RNIMOA incorporates key features from red-necking, including a velocity modulation mechanism mimicking the snake's burst-and-glide motion, a position update rule based on proximity to the optimal solution, and a population diversity preservation strategy. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a theoretical analysis of its convergence properties and its potential for adapting to different problem landscapes. The aim is to provide a robust and efficient optimization technique with potential applications in various fields.

title: ## Grey-Tail Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GT-MHOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Grey-Tail Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (GT-MHOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Grey-tailed Fish Eagle (Eleutherornis griseicauda). The algorithm leverages the eagle's unique hunting strategy – utilizing visual acuity and strategic positioning – to navigate a search space and find optimal solutions. GT-MHOA incorporates a 'scanning' mechanism mimicking the eagle's eye movements, a 'territorial defense' strategy based on competitive positioning, and a 'gradient-following' component inspired by the eagle's preference for areas with higher prey concentration. The algorithm's core components include a dynamic scanning radius, a competitive positioning scheme based on distance and relative fitness, and a gradient-driven movement strategy. While this paper focuses on the algorithm's theoretical framework and design, it lays the groundwork for potential future experimental validation and comparison with existing metaheuristic methods. The goal is to create an algorithm that is adaptable, efficient, and capable of effectively exploring complex search spaces.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应参数调整
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize parameter adjustment in machine learning models. Traditional parameter adjustment methods often rely on iterative refinement, which can be slow and computationally expensive. We propose a novel approach leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust parameters during the training process, potentially accelerating learning and improving model performance. This work investigates the feasibility of using entangled states to facilitate faster and more efficient search, offering a fundamentally different paradigm for parameter optimization. We outline the theoretical framework, describe the implementation of the quantum entanglement-based mechanism, and present preliminary results demonstrating a significant improvement in learning speed compared to classical methods. The core claim is that this approach, leveraging quantum entanglement, provides a new and potentially transformative mechanism for parameter optimization, offering a pathway towards more sophisticated and efficient machine learning models.

abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to quantum topology optimization, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum spacetime to achieve more efficient quantum communication and computation. Traditional methods often rely on handcrafted designs, while our algorithm directly optimizes the quantum topology, providing greater flexibility and potential for enhanced performance. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the topological structure of spacetime to guide the optimization process, resulting in improved quantum entanglement and information transfer. We explore the potential benefits of this method for quantum technologies.

title: Allegheny Woodrat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AWIMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Allegheny Woodrat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AWIMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Allegheny Woodrat. The algorithm leverages the woodrat's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies, specifically its habit of caching food in a spatially distributed manner with a bias towards promising locations, to guide the search process in optimization problems. AWIMA incorporates a novel adaptive memory mechanism, mimicking the woodrat's ability to remember and revisit high-reward areas. The algorithm's core components include an initial population generation, an evaluation function based on a modified distance metric, a mutation operator inspired by the woodrat's foraging path, and an adaptive learning rate scheme. We demonstrate the effectiveness of AWIMA on several benchmark optimization problems, including the Sphere function, Rastrigin function, and the Powell's test functions. The results indicate that AWIMA consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in problems with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. The key contribution of this work lies in the innovative application of the Allegheny Woodrat's natural behavior to inspire a robust and efficient metaheuristic optimization algorithm. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence speed, solution quality, and computational cost.

title: 数字智能技术赋能民办高校英语课程生态的价值意蕴与优化向度研究
abstract: 教育数字化转型是新时代高等教育高质量发展的核心驱动力，民办高校英语课程作为公共基础课程，其传统课程生态已难以适配应用型人才培养需求。本文以课程生态理论为分析框架，从教学主体、课程内容、教学场景、评价机制四个维度剖析民办高校英语课程生态的现实失衡表现，阐释数字智能技术赋能课程生态的多维价值意蕴，梳理技术落地的现实阻滞因素，进而从主体能力、内容建设、场景融合、制度保障四个层面提出优化向度，为民办高校英语课程数字化转型提供理论参考。

title: A Machine Learning-Based UPI Security and Fraud Detection
abstract: Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has revolutionized digital payments in India, enabling seamless, real-time money transfers between accounts. However, its growing popularity has made it increasingly susceptible to fraudulent activities such as phishing, account takeovers, and transaction manipulation. This study introduces a hybrid fraud detection system integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Autoencoder, Local Outlier Factor (LOF), and K-Means Clustering to detect anomalous UPI transactions efficiently. The system utilizes anonymized UPI transaction data including transaction amount, time, device identifiers, and geolocation. Preprocessing involved encoding categorical features, normalizing numerical variables, and addressing missing data. The proposed hybrid approach was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC metrics, achieving higher accuracy and fewer false positives compared to traditional methods. The findings highlight that deep learning combined with unsupervised techniques offers a robust solution for ensuring secure and reliable UPI payment operations.

title: The cost of an aggregation rule when texts and individual judgements are both available: a preregistered multiverse on RP-Mod & RP-Crowd
abstract: This project preregisters a multiverse analysis of annotation aggregation on RP-Mod & RP-Crowd, a German news comment corpus that publishes both the comment texts and the individual judgements behind each label, alongside professional moderators' decisions. A published corpus label is not an observation but the output of a decision about how to collapse several annotators' judgements into one, and that decision is rarely reported. Earlier work by the author on DeTox, a corpus that releases its judgements but not its texts, found the share of comments labelled hate speech ranging from 0.038 to 0.295 across defensible aggregation rules, and from 0.051 to 0.145 across the subset of rules with published precedent. Because DeTox ships no texts, that analysis could not establish the consequence that matters most to the field: whether the choice moves the performance figure a paper reports. RP-Mod & RP-Crowd permits that step. The study crosses six declared axes — aggregation function, threshold on the mean, tie resolution, annotation depth, treatment of items the annotators split on, and the choice between crowd and moderator as ground truth — and reports, for every resulting specification, the share of items labelled positive, Krippendorff's alpha on the individual judgements, the number of items retained, and the cross-validated F1 of a deterministic classifier trained on one specification and evaluated against another. All specifications share one fold plan, so the fold-to-fold spread of the same pipeline serves as the noise floor against which every difference is read. Four directional hypotheses are stated in advance, each with an explicit disconfirming outcome, and the specification grid is fixed before the data are downloaded. At the time of registration no file from the dataset has been accessed; only the public record page has been seen. Expected outcome: the aggregation choice moves both the reported prevalence and the reported F1 by more than the noise of the pipeline, with the treatment of disagreement as the largest single contributor.

title: A tailings dam safety question answering framework integrating a knowledge graph with retrieval augmented generation
abstract: Tailings dam accidents pose serious threats to public safety and economic stability, creating a strong demand for intelligent information systems that can support emergency response and safety management. To address this challenge, this study proposes TSA-KA, a domain-specific question-answering framework for tailings dam safety that integrates structured knowledge representation with retrieval-augmented response generation. The framework first constructs a knowledge graph from emergency response plans and related domain documents to provide standardized and reliable knowledge support. To improve query understanding, an intent recognition model based on RoBERTa-TextCNN with an attention mechanism is developed to capture fine-grained semantic patterns in user questions. In addition, a retrieval-augmented generation module is introduced, in which ChatGLM3-6B is fine-tuned using low-rank adaptation to generate contextually appropriate and domain-consistent responses. The novelty of TSA-KA lies in the integration of a tailings-dam-safety knowledge graph, intent recognition, evidence retrieval, and retrieval-augmented generation into a unified domain-specific question-answering framework. The constructed knowledge graph contains 21 entity categories, 23 relation categories, 2,911 entities, and 20,146 relations/triples, and the question-answering experiments were conducted on 2,346 manually constructed question-answer pairs. The RoBERTa-TextCNN-Attention intent recognition model achieved an Aggregate F1 score of 94.12%, while the LoRA-adapted ChatGLM3-6B configuration achieved RAGAS scores of 0.89, 0.82, and 0.87 for answer relevancy, faithfulness, and context precision, respectively, on the common held-out comparative evaluation set. These results suggest that integrating structured domain knowledge with retrieval-augmented generation is a feasible way to improve domain relevance, evidence grounding, and contextual consistency in tailings dam safety question answering.

title: Do VLMs Share Safety Neurons Across Modalities?
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can comply with harmful requests delivered through images, even when their LLM backbones would refuse the same content in text. While prior work characterizes these jailbreaks empirically or at the representation level, how visual inputs perturb safety pathways at the neuron level remains uncharted. We close this gap with a causal, neuron-level analysis of safety mechanisms in 10 VLMs. We propose a two-stage detection pipeline with iterative ablation that accounts for self-repair, and introduce two modality-isolated benchmarks, ViSafe-Detect and ViSafe-Eval, which decouple visual and textual safety signals. Our analysis reveals: (i) Text safety in VLMs is localizable: $\sim$88 neurons ($<$0.01%) whose targeted ablation substantially reduces refusal. (ii) Text safety neurons constitute the dominant refusal pathway: ablating them is the only intervention that consistently and substantially reduces refusal across all models. (iii) Visual safety is high-dimensional and diffuse at the single-neuron level: text safety concentrates in $\sim$5 subspace directions while visual safety requires $\geq$50. This gap holds across architectures, explaining why current alignment has not closed the visual safety gap. Project page is at: https://jiaxuan-li.github.io/vlm-safety-neuron/ Warning: this paper may include examples of harmful content.

title: Geometry of Divergence: Tracking Hidden-State Trajectories for Adaptive Multi-Turn Reasoning
abstract: LLM agents need to sustain goal-consistent reasoning across long multi-turn interactions under strict resource constraints. However, as the multi-turn context accumulates, it can destabilize the underlying LLM's internal representation of task-relevant information from earlier turns, blurring the boundary between constructive reasoning and representation drift. We formulate multi-turn reasoning as a hidden-state trajectory of the underlying LLM that is characterized via two complementary signals: temporal curvature that captures the directional consistency of turn-to-turn updates, and variance slope which measures the expansion or contraction of the exploration space. Across four tasks and three underlying LLMs, we observed that these geometric signals distinguish between correct and incorrect episodes prior to completion. We further decompose each episode into three-action chains formed from four actions (Read, Write, Respond, Transfer) and show that separability is action-dependent, with different signals distinguishing various chain patterns. Our experiments demonstrate that trajectory geometry can identify critical turns in the reasoning process, increasing task success rates on $τ$-Bench from 24.1% to 39.6% while reducing token cost by 11.2%.

title: BCPPO: Bachelier-Inspired Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization for Tail-Risk-Aware Safe Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Expected-cost constraints can still permit rare, high-cost events. Monte Carlo conditional value at risk (CVaR) gradients can be noisy at high confidence, whereas critics that model an outcome distribution add complexity. We propose BCPPO (Bachelier-Inspired Constrained Proximal Policy Optimization), a proximal policy optimization (PPO) method. Separately initialized cost-prediction networks (critics), trained with random sample masks, produce disagreement that marks predictions sensitive to which state-action regions occur in the training data and to critic training. A Bachelier formula for the expected amount above a reference level converts this disagreement into a smooth policy-update penalty. Gradients from this penalty do not alter the critics, so temporal-difference (TD) critic learning is unchanged. A saturation-aware controller adjusts the mean-cost penalty and stops accumulated error from growing while that penalty is clipped. Deployment retains only the policy network. The disagreement penalty is neither a tail-event probability nor a guaranteed error bound, and it provides no safety guarantee. Across 175 runs with shared tasks, costs, budgets, training steps, and evaluation seeds, no comparator attains both higher mean return and lower mean CVaR than BCPPO in any task. On Push1, BCPPO has no lower return and no higher CVaR than every comparator, with at least one strict gain. These results support a practical balance among reward, caution around cost predictions that vary across trained critics, and policy-only deployment.

title: Aspire: Can Models Self-Evolve from Vague Goals?
abstract: Many important forms of human learning begin with a vague goal, such as "become a better physicist" or "improve at research." Learners must interpret the goal, identify capability gaps, decide how to learn, and determine whether they have actually improved. In contrast, existing work on LLM self-evolution typically begins with tasks and evaluation metrics specified by humans, reducing self-evolution to optimizing an explicit objective rather than deciding what and how to learn. We introduce ASPIRE, a benchmark for vague-goal-driven self-evolution. ASPIRE provides only a natural-language capability goal while downstream evaluation tasks remain hidden. The agent must operationalize the goal by choosing data and update methods, constructing training and validation signals, and deciding when to evaluate. ASPIRE supports both model-weight and agent-harness evolution in a unified interactive environment and evaluates the resulting systems on a hidden, expert-authored set of 520 items spanning six goals. Our experiments show that vague goals redirect search effort toward goal interpretation. Current agents routinely complete training and harness-editing loops, but weight-level gains remain sparse and unstable, and the strongest evolved harness remains below the engineered Qwen-Agent reference. Agents often train on mismatched data and trust narrow self-evaluations, so local gains fail to transfer to hidden evaluation and continued search and training can erase earlier improvements.

title: Not All Fallbacks Are Failures: Understanding and Recovering from Fallbacks in Mobile Voice Assistants
abstract: Robust understanding of user input is a core requirement for voice assistants deployed in real-world environments. In practice, these systems encounter heterogeneous fallback situations caused by noisy audio input, transcription errors, ambiguous requests, incomplete utterances, or unintended activations. Existing systems typically respond with generic fallback messages, which do not resolve the underlying interaction failure and can degrade user experience. We study fallback handling in a deployed smartwatch-based voice assistant for general health support in everyday environments. Our analysis is based on six months of real-world usage data from more than 500 users, yielding a dataset of 3,030 anonymized, naturally occurring fallback-triggering utterances. We contribute (1) an operational taxonomy and the annotated VoxFallbacks dataset of these interactions, (2) a comparative evaluation of different models within a classification pipeline under practical deployment constraints, and (3) practical lessons for designing robust and cost-efficient fallback mechanisms. Results show that lightweight embedding-based classifiers outperform larger generative models on most classification tasks while requiring substantially fewer computational resources.

title: Bridging the Data Gap: LLM-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Natural Language Inference
abstract: This thesis addresses the challenge of data scarcity in low-resource languages by leveraging the dual role of Large Language Models (LLMs) to both generate and annotate data. We evaluate the reliability of LLM-based annotations and examine the effectiveness of LLM-generated synthetic data in improving downstream task performance. This research uses the Natural Language Inference (NLI) task in Farsi as its case study. Our approach involves benchmarking both open-weight and closed-source LLMs on a gold-standard dataset, developing an LLM-driven pipeline to generate labeled premise-hypothesis pairs, and training mT5 models to measure performance gains. Further experiments were conducted with various LLM annotators to analyze how annotation quality affects model outcomes. The results reveal key insights. First, synthetic data substantially improves model performance, particularly under sequential training regimes, confirming its effectiveness as a strategy for data augmentation in low-resource settings. Second, the quality of annotations plays a decisive role in downstream outcomes—higher-quality labels consistently lead to greater accuracy and robustness. Finally, the reliability of an LLM as an annotator emerges as a multifaceted property, shaped by factors including model architecture, prompt design, and the inherent complexity of the task itself. These findings show that while LLM-generated synthetic data can mitigate data scarcity issues, annotation quality remains a critical factor influencing model performance. evidence.title: Bridging the Data Gap: LLM-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Low-Resource Natural Language Inference
evidence.abstract: This thesis addresses the challenge of data scarcity in low-resource languages by leveraging the dual role of Large Language Models (LLMs) to both generate and annotate data. We evaluate the reliability of LLM-based annotations and examine the effectiveness of LLM-generated synthetic data in improving downstream task performance. This research uses the Natural Language Inference (NLI) task in Farsi as its case study. These findings show that while LLM-generated synthetic data can mitigate data scarcity issues, annotation quality remains a critical factor influencing model performance. The thesis contributes insights into optimizing annotation pipelines and synthetic data utility for low-resource NLP, with implications for multilingual model training strategies.

title: Novel Entropy-Based Framework for Quantifying Dynamic Epistemic Uncertainty in Clinical Medicine
abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of clinical large language models (LLMs) introduces significant risks of automation bias, premature closure, and clinician deskilling. Current interpretability paradigms, including latent space trajectories, Concept Activation Vectors, and Concept Bottleneck Models, suffer from topological stagnation, metric distortion, and epistemic occlusion, frequently masking intermediate diagnostic uncertainty behind falsely confident outputs. To address these structural vulnerabilities, this paper introduces a novel closed-loop, multi-agent framework designed to quantify and visualize dynamic epistemic uncertainty in clinical LLM reasoning. By coupling predictive Shannon entropy with non-linear Isometric Feature Mapping (ISOMAP), the architecture projects high-dimensional inference state vectors onto a calibrated two-dimensional latent space, thereby assigning a quantifiable thermodynamic energy state to the reasoning path to track diagnostic velocity, cognitive momentum, and trajectory efficiency across sequential diagnostic rounds. Pilot validation across representative emergency medicine scenarios demonstrated distinct topological and information-theoretic behaviors: unconfounded cases (cerebellar infarction) exhibited smooth geodesic progression toward the ground truth alongside monotonic Shannon entropy decay from 2.15 to 1.74; noisy environments with ambiguous findings (spontaneous pneumothorax) suffered from trajectory wandering, local minimum traps, and high sustained entropy (~2.41) due to insufficient repulsive weighting for negative evidence; and triage-conflicted cases (acute cholangitis) achieved precise geometric proximity to the true node but experienced top-1 rank stagnation because the model conflated acute severity triage (sepsis) with anatomical etiology. By rendering machine hesitation and cognitive divergence visually auditable before final diagnostic crystallization, this geometric-information framework enables dynamic trust calibration and human-AI co-regulation at the point of care while establishing a clear mathematical foundation for future architectural interventions, such as dual-channel safety decoupling and non-linear repulsive weighting. Moving forward, validating these architectural enhancements across large-scale electronic health record databases and prospective clinical trials will be essential to realize its full clinical utility, establishing a foundational blueprint for safe, transparent, and cognitively synergistic AI integration in future medical practice. By rendering the LLM’s reasoning process visually auditable, this framework lays the groundwork for capturing and externalizing the clinician’s own cognitive patterns within the AI, forming a coupled system. This enables the explicit visualization of cognitive gaps between physician hypotheses and AI inferences, transforming the interaction from simple answer-checking into a dynamic learning process for both human and machine that prevents diagnostic oversight. Ultimately, because the responsibility for final clinical decision-making remains with the human practitioner, this framework serves as a vital decision-support mechanism. Moving forward, validating these architectural enhancements across large-scale electronic health record databases and prospective clinical trials will be essential to realize its full clinical utility, establishing a foundational blueprint for safe, transparent, and cognitively synergistic AI integration in future medical practice.

title: AI-EMPOWERED TEACHING REFORM AND PRACTICAL PATH EXPLORATION FOR THE “GEOLOGY” COURSE
abstract: In response to the prevalent issues in traditional geology instruction—namely, the abstract nature of theoretical content, the limited relevance to safety engineering practices, and the insufficient alignment with the talent development demands of intelligent mining engineering—this study focuses on the emerging trends of intelligent mining and geological digitization. It investigates the reform of geology course teaching empowered by artificial intelligence. The proposed reform restructures the course content system, integrates AI technologies to innovate pedagogical models, introduces AI-based intelligent mineral generation techniques, and implements virtual mineral cognition experiments, thereby addressing the deficiencies in traditional experimental teaching resources. By establishing an intelligent teaching system and innovative experimental projects, the conventional rote-teaching model has been effectively transformed, resulting in notable improvements in classroom teaching quality and students’ knowledge internalization efficiency. Students’ competencies in intelligent geological analysis, accurate disaster assessment, and innovative mining engineering practices have been strengthened, alongside enhanced innovative thinking and overall professional proficiency. This reform aligns with the objectives of intelligent mining talent cultivation and offers valuable reference and insights for the intelligent teaching reform of geology courses in mining-related disciplines.

title: LSTM-Based Daily Power Forecasting for a 1 MWp PV System in Tropical Indonesia: Toward Operational Optimization
abstract: Variations in solar irradiance and module temperature significantly affect the performance and operational efficiency of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power systems, especially in tropical regions. This study investigates the application of a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network for accurate real-time power prediction in a 1 MWp PV power plant at Institut Teknologi Sumatera (ITERA), Indonesia. Unlike traditional approaches and conventional artificial neural networks (ANN), LSTM networks can effectively capture long-term temporal dependencies and highly nonlinear patterns in PV output data. A five-minute resolution dataset, including actual power output, solar irradiance, and module temperature, was collected throughout March 2025 for model training, with validation performed using independent data from April. The developed LSTM model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 42.8 kW (approximately 4–6% of maximum plant capacity) and a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.84 during active hours (05:00–19:00) on the validation dataset. These findings indicate that the model performs well not only on the training data, but also maintains strong generalization to unfamiliar data. The proposed approach enables reliable real-time power prediction, supporting applications such as energy forecasting, inverter control, dispatch planning, and anomaly detection in PV systems. This work provides a practical and scalable solution for improving the adaptability and integration of solar power plants in dynamic tropical environments, contributing to the advancement of AI-driven sustainable energy systems.

title: A MACHINE LEARNING-BASED CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR AUTOMATED DIGITAL WASTE CLASSIFICATION WITH PROJECTED CARBON FOOTPRINT REDUCTION
abstract: Pertumbuhan volume data digital yang pesat turut meningkatkan proporsi sampah digital serta berkontribusi terhadap emisi karbon pusat data, sementara penelitian klasifikasi berkas yang ada umumnya belum menghubungkan hasil klasifikasi dengan estimasi dampak lingkungan secara terukur. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengusulkan Automated Digital Waste Classification (ADWC), sebuah kerangka kerja konseptual berbasis pembelajaran mesin. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan Design Science Research (DSR) dengan evaluasi kelayakan artefak melalui sintesis literatur dan proyeksi berbasis benchmark, mencakup arsitektur lima lapisan yang mengintegrasikan fitur metadata. Hasil proyeksi menunjukkan bahwa konfigurasi penuh ADWC mencapai macro-F1 tertinggi melampaui konfigurasi fitur tunggal maupun kombinasi parsial, serta kompetitif terhadap model benchmark termutakhir seperti CNN-BERT Hybrid. Pada korpus asumsi ±30 TB, ADWC-Full diproyeksikan mengidentifikasi 38,7% data sebagai limbah digital yang dapat ditindaklanjuti, dengan potensi reduksi emisi karbon yang meningkat proporsional terhadap skala implementasi. Analisis sensitivitas mengungkap bahwa intensitas karbon jaringan listrik merupakan parameter paling berpengaruh terhadap besarnya manfaat lingkungan jauh melampaui pengaruh PUE, intensitas energi penyimpanan, maupun fraksi limbah teridentifikasi. Temuan ini menegaskan kelayakan konseptual ADWC sebagai kerangka kerja yang menghubungkan tata kelola data pada tingkat berkas dengan indikator keberlanjutan yang terukur meskipun seluruh hasil masih bersifat proyeksi berbasis benchmark dan memerlukan validasi empiris pada lingkungan operasional nyata.

title: Adaptive ZKP Selection Framework for Privacy-Preserving Decentralized Identity Using DID and Verifiable Credentials
abstract: The rapid growth of digital services has increased the demand for identity systems that provide strong authentication while minimizing unnecessary disclosure of personal information. Conventional identity management architectures generally depend on centralized identity providers and frequently require users to disclose complete identity attributes even when a service requires only a limited assertion. Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and Verifiable Credentials (VCs) provide an alternative model in which identity holders can manage cryptographically verifiable credentials independently of a centralized identity provider. However, the privacy guarantees of decentralized identity systems depend substantially on the cryptographic proof mechanism used during credential presentation. Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) enable a prover to demonstrate knowledge of a secret or the validity of a statement without revealing the underlying secret. Different ZKP and selective-disclosure mechanisms exhibit significantly different characteristics with respect to proof size, generation time, verification time, communication overhead, computational requirements, privacy guarantees, interoperability, and implementation complexity. Consequently, selecting a single proof mechanism for every decentralized identity scenario can result in unnecessary computational cost or inadequate privacy protection. This paper proposes an Adaptive ZKP Selection Framework (AZSF) for privacy-preserving decentralized identity using DIDs and Verifiable Credentials. The framework dynamically selects an appropriate proof mechanism according to the privacy sensitivity of requested attributes, disclosure requirements, verifier trust conditions, computational resources, proof-generation latency, communication constraints, interoperability requirements, and unlinkability requirements. The proposed architecture introduces a policy-driven decision layer between the credential wallet and proof-generation subsystem. It evaluates candidate mechanisms including selective-disclosure signatures, BBS-based proofs, SD-JWT-based selective disclosure, and general-purpose succinct zero-knowledge proof systems such as zk-SNARK/PLONK-style approaches. A formal multi-criteria decision model is developed to represent the selection process. The framework defines privacy, performance, communication, interoperability, and deployment criteria and computes an adaptive suitability score for each candidate proof mechanism. A threat model covering credential theft, replay, correlation, malicious verifiers, issuer compromise, metadata leakage, and proof substitution is presented. The paper further proposes an experimental methodology for evaluating proof generation time, verification time, proof size, communication overhead, privacy leakage, unlinkability, and resource consumption. The proposed framework provides a systematic foundation for choosing cryptographic proof mechanisms according to application requirements instead of adopting a one-size-fits-all approach. Index Terms— Decentralized Identity, Decentralized Identifiers, Verifiable Credentials, Zero-Knowledge Proofs, Privacy-Preserving Identity, Selective Disclosure, BBS Signatures, SD-JWT, Self-Sovereign Identity, Privacy Engineering, Adaptive Cryptography.
